A string attached to a flying kite is 200 m long, and its angle of elevation is 60 degrees. Find the height of the kite above the hand, taking the string to be fully stretched..

Worked Example: 1. Find the angle of elevation in the following figures: (i) vertical side k, base √(3)k.

Formula used: Sketch the triangle, mark the elevation/depression angle, then use tan (or sin/cos) with the known side.

Step 1: tan theta = k/(√(3)k) = 1/√(3).

Step 2: theta = tan^-1(1/√(3)).

Answer: theta = 30 degrees.

Worked Example: 2. Find the angle of depression in the following figures (the angle of depression equals the angle at the ground by alternate angles): (i) vertical side 5 cm, base 6 cm.

Formula used: Sketch the triangle, mark the elevation/depression angle, then use tan (or sin/cos) with the known side.

Step 1: tan theta = 5/6 = 0.8333.

Step 2: theta = tan^-1(0.8333).

Answer: theta = 39.8 degrees (approx).

Worked Example: 3. A balloon is connected to a meteorological ground station by a cable of length 215 m inclined at 60 degrees to the horizontal. Determine the height of the balloon from the earth.

Formula used: Sketch the triangle, mark the elevation/depression angle, then use tan (or sin/cos) with the known side.

Step 1: height = 215 x sin 60 degrees.

Step 2: 215 x √(3)/2 = 215 x 0.8660.

Answer: height = 186.20 m (approx).

Worked Example: 4. The angle of elevation of the top of a tower at a distance of 150 meters from its foot on a horizontal plane is found to be 30 degrees. Find the height of the tower.

Formula used: Sketch the triangle, mark the elevation/depression angle, then use tan (or sin/cos) with the known side.

Step 1: height = 150 x tan 30 degrees.

Step 2: 150 x (1/√(3)) = 150 x 0.5774.

Answer: height = 86.60 m (approx).

Worked Example: 7. From the top of a cliff, 201 m high, the angle of depression of the top and bottom of a tower are observed to be 30 degrees and 60 degrees. Find the height of the tower.

Formula used: Sketch the triangle, mark the elevation/depression angle, then use tan (or sin/cos) with the known side.

Step 1: let the distance be d and the tower height be h.

Step 2: tan 60 degrees = 201/d, so d = 201/√(3).

Step 3: tan 30 degrees = (201 - h)/d, so 201 - h = d x tan 30 degrees = (201/√(3)) x (1/√(3)) = 201/3 = 67.

Step 4: h = 201 - 67.

Answer: height of the tower = 134 m.

mcqs.q: In a figure the vertical side is k and the base is sqrt(3)k. Find the angle of elevation theta.
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = k/(sqrt(3)k) = 1/sqrt(3), so theta = tan^-1(1/sqrt(3)) = 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: In a figure the vertical side is 5 cm and the base is 6 cm. Find the angle of depression.
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = 5/6 = 0.8333, so theta = tan^-1(0.8333) = 39.8 degrees approx.

mcqs.q: A balloon is held by a cable of length 215 m inclined at 60 degrees to the horizontal. Find the height of the balloon.
mcqs.why: Working: height = 215 x sin 60 degrees = 215 x sqrt(3)/2 = 215 x 0.8660 = 186.20 m approx.

mcqs.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower at a distance of 150 m from its foot is 30 degrees. Find the height of the tower.
mcqs.why: Working: height = 150 x tan 30 degrees = 150 x (1/sqrt(3)) = 150 x 0.5774 = 86.60 m approx.

mcqs.q: From the top of a cliff 201 m high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a tower are 30 degrees and 60 degrees. Find the height of the tower.
mcqs.why: Working: tan 60 = 201/d gives d = 201/sqrt(3); 201 - h = d x tan 30 = 201/3 = 67, so h = 201 - 67 = 134 m.

mcqs.q: A kite string is 200 m long and its angle of elevation is 60 degrees. Find the height of the kite above the hand.
mcqs.why: Working: height = 200 x sin 60 degrees = 200 x 0.8660 = 173.20 m approx, taking the string as fully stretched.

mcqs.q: An observer 1.5 m tall is 20 m away from a tower 30 m high. Find the angle of elevation from his eye to the top of the tower.
mcqs.why: Working: height above eye level = 30 - 1.5 = 28.5 m; tan theta = 28.5/20 = 1.425, so theta = tan^-1(1.425) = 54.94 degrees approx.

mcqs.q: The angle of depression of a 37 m high building from the top of a tower 117 m high is 38 degrees. Find the distance between the building and the tower.
mcqs.why: Working: height difference = 117 - 37 = 80 m; tan 38 degrees = 80/d, so d = 80 / tan 38 degrees = 80 / 0.7813 = 102.40 m approx.

mcqs.q: The angle of elevation of a tower from a point is 30 degrees. On walking 100 m towards the tower it becomes 60 degrees. Find the height of the tower.
mcqs.why: Working: with distance x from the nearer point, h = x tan 60 and h = (x + 100) tan 30; solving gives x = 50 and h = 50 x sqrt(3) = 86.60 m approx.

mcqs.q: Why does an angle of depression problem become a right-angled triangle with the angle at the ground?
options: The two angles are always 90 degrees
The line of sight is always vertical
The depression angle at the top equals the elevation angle at the bottom by alternate angles
mcqs.why: The angle of depression at the top equals the angle of elevation at the bottom by alternate angles between parallel horizontals.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4 (pp.139-140) - Proving Trigonometric Identities
lessons.notes_html:
To prove an identity, work on the more complicated side and turn it into the other side. The standard moves are: write everything in sin and cos; use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (and 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta, 1 + cot^2 theta = cosec^2 theta); combine fractions over a common denominator; and multiply top and bottom by a conjugate such as (1 + sin theta). The last questions run the identities backwards: given one ratio (sin theta = 4/5, for example), find all the others from the three identities.

Formula: sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 ; 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta ; 1 + cot^2 theta = cosec^2 theta

In this exercise: 1. Prove: (1 - tan^2 theta)/(1 + tan^2 theta) = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta.. 2. Prove: sin theta/(sec theta - 1) + sin theta/(sec theta + 1) = 2 cot theta.. 3. Prove: sin theta/(cosec theta - cot theta) = 1 + cos theta.. 4. Prove: cos theta/(1 + sin theta) = (1 - sin theta)/cos theta.. 5. Prove: (sin theta - 2 sin^3 theta)/(2 cos^3 theta - cos theta) = tan theta.. 6. Prove: (tan theta - cot theta)/(sin theta cos theta) = tan^2 theta - cot^2 theta.. 7. Prove: cos theta/(1 - sin theta) + cos theta/(1 + sin theta) = 2 sec theta.. 8. Prove: cos theta/(cosec theta + 1) + cos theta/(cosec theta - 1) = 2 tan theta.. 9. Prove: sin theta/(1 - cos theta) + tan theta/(1 + cos theta) = sec theta cosec theta + cot theta.. 10. Prove: √((1 - sin theta)/(1 + sin theta)) = sec theta - tan theta.. 11. Prove: (1 + cos theta)/(1 - cos theta) = (cosec theta + cot theta)^2.. 12. Prove: (1 + tan^2 theta)(1 - sin theta)(1 + sin theta) = 1.. 13. Prove: 1/(sec theta - tan theta) = sec theta + tan theta.. 14. Prove: √((1 + sin theta)/(1 - sin theta)) + √((1 - sin theta)/(1 + sin theta)) = 2 sec theta.. 15. If sin theta = 4/5, then find the remaining trigonometric ratios using trigonometric identities. (Acute theta.). 16. If tan theta = 1/√(3), then find the remaining trigonometric ratios. (Acute theta.). 17. If cos theta = 1/2, then find. 18. A surveyor stands on level ground and observes the top of a tower at an angle theta. If the distance from the surveyor to the tower is 12 m and the height of the tower is 5 m, use the identity 1 + cot^2 theta = cosec^2 theta to find cosec theta.. 19. A ladder leans against a wall making an angle theta with the ground. If the ratio of the height of the wall to the base of the ladder is 3:4, find the value of sec theta using the identity 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta..

Worked Example: 1. Prove: (1 - tan^2 theta)/(1 + tan^2 theta) = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta.

Formula used: Change to sin and cos, combine fractions, and use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (or its two partners).

Step 1: multiply numerator and denominator by cos^2 theta.

Step 2: (1 - tan^2 theta) x cos^2 theta = cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta.

Step 3: (1 + tan^2 theta) x cos^2 theta = cos^2 theta + sin^2 theta = 1.

Step 4: the ratio is cos^2 theta - sin^2 theta. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 3. Prove: sin theta/(cosec theta - cot theta) = 1 + cos theta.

Formula used: Change to sin and cos, combine fractions, and use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (or its two partners).

Step 1: cosec theta - cot theta = (1 - cos theta)/sin theta.

Step 2: sin theta divided by (1 - cos theta)/sin theta = sin^2 theta/(1 - cos theta).

Step 3: sin^2 theta = 1 - cos^2 theta = (1 - cos theta)(1 + cos theta).

Step 4: cancelling (1 - cos theta) gives 1 + cos theta. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 10. Prove: √((1 - sin theta)/(1 + sin theta)) = sec theta - tan theta.

Formula used: Change to sin and cos, combine fractions, and use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (or its two partners).

Step 1: multiply inside the root by (1 - sin theta)/(1 - sin theta): (1 - sin theta)^2/(1 - sin^2 theta) = (1 - sin theta)^2/cos^2 theta.

Step 2: square root = (1 - sin theta)/cos theta = sec theta - tan theta (for cos theta positive). Hence proved.

Worked Example: 13. Prove: 1/(sec theta - tan theta) = sec theta + tan theta.

Formula used: Change to sin and cos, combine fractions, and use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (or its two partners).

Step 1: multiply numerator and denominator by (sec theta + tan theta).

Step 2: denominator = sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta = 1.

Step 3: the result is sec theta + tan theta. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 15. If sin theta = 4/5, then find the remaining trigonometric ratios using trigonometric identities. (Acute theta.)

Formula used: Change to sin and cos, combine fractions, and use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (or its two partners).

Step 1: cos theta = √(1 - sin^2 theta) = √(1 - 16/25) = 3/5.

Step 2: tan theta = sin theta/cos theta = 4/3.

Step 3: cosec theta = 5/4, sec theta = 5/3, cot theta = 3/4.

Answer: cos = 3/5, tan = 4/3, cosec = 5/4, sec = 5/3, cot = 3/4.

Worked Example: 18. A surveyor stands on level ground and observes the top of a tower at an angle theta. If the distance from the surveyor to the tower is 12 m and the height of the tower is 5 m, use the identity 1 + cot^2 theta = cosec^2 theta to find cosec theta.

Formula used: Change to sin and cos, combine fractions, and use sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (or its two partners).

Step 1: tan theta = 5/12, so cot theta = 12/5.

Step 2: cosec^2 theta = 1 + cot^2 theta = 1 + 144/25 = 169/25.

Step 3: cosec theta = 13/5.

Answer: cosec theta = 13/5.

mcqs.q: Which identity is the basic identity used in almost every proof in this unit?
mcqs.why: The basic identity is sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1, together with 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta and 1 + cot^2 theta = cosec^2 theta.

mcqs.q: If sin theta = 4/5 for acute theta, find cos theta.
mcqs.why: Working: cos theta = sqrt(1 - sin^2 theta) = sqrt(1 - 16/25) = sqrt(9/25) = 3/5.

mcqs.q: If sin theta = 4/5 and cos theta = 3/5, find tan theta.
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = sin theta / cos theta = (4/5) / (3/5) = 4/3.

mcqs.q: If sin theta = 4/5 for acute theta, find cosec theta.
mcqs.why: Working: cosec theta = 1 / sin theta = 1 / (4/5) = 5/4.

mcqs.q: A surveyor is 12 m from a tower of height 5 m. Using 1 + cot^2 theta = cosec^2 theta, find cosec theta.
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = 5/12 so cot theta = 12/5; cosec^2 theta = 1 + 144/25 = 169/25, so cosec theta = 13/5.

mcqs.q: In the surveyor example with distance 12 m and tower height 5 m, what is cot theta?
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = height/distance = 5/12, so cot theta = 1 / tan theta = 12/5.

mcqs.q: If tan theta = 1/sqrt(3) for acute theta, find cos theta.
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = 1/sqrt(3) is the 30-degree ratio, with opposite 1, adjacent sqrt(3), hypotenuse 2, so cos theta = sqrt(3)/2.

mcqs.q: If cos theta = 1/2 for acute theta, find tan theta.
mcqs.why: Working: sin theta = sqrt(1 - 1/4) = sqrt(3)/2; tan theta = sin theta / cos theta = (sqrt(3)/2) / (1/2) = sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: A ladder makes angle theta with the ground and the ratio of wall height to ladder base is 3:4. Using 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta, find sec theta.
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = 3/4, so sec^2 theta = 1 + tan^2 theta = 1 + 9/16 = 25/16, giving sec theta = 5/4.

mcqs.q: To prove 1/(sec theta - tan theta) = sec theta + tan theta, multiplying top and bottom by (sec theta + tan theta) makes the denominator equal to what?
mcqs.why: Working: denominator becomes sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta = 1 by the identity 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta, leaving sec theta + tan theta.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.5 (pp.145-146) - Bearings
lessons.notes_html:
A bearing is measured clockwise from the north line at the point you stand on, and is written with three figures. North = 000, east = 090, south = 180, west = 270. Descriptions such as "33 degrees east of north" or "28 degrees south of east" are converted by starting from the named cardinal point and adding or subtracting as the direction turns. The back bearing (the bearing of the starting point from the end point) is the forward bearing + 180 (subtract 360 if the result passes 360). In figure questions, the interior angles of the triangle plus parallel north lines give the turns.

Formula: Back bearing = forward bearing + 180 degrees (mod 360)

In this exercise: 1. The figure shows the positions of O, A, B, C and D. A is 33 degrees east of north, B is 28 degrees south of east, C is 44 degrees south of west, D is 39 degrees west of north. Find the bearing of. 2. The figure shows the position of P, A, B and C. A is 35 degrees north of east, B is 15 degrees east of south, C is 47 degrees north of west. Find the bearing of. 3. The figure shows the positions of P, Q and R. At P, PR is 36 degrees from north and PQ is 37 degrees from PR; at R the interior angle PRQ is 100 degrees. Find the bearing of. 4. A, B, C and D are the four corners of a rectangular plot marked out on level ground. Given that the bearing of B from A is 040 degrees and that the bearing of C from A is 090 degrees, find the bearing of. 5. P, Q and R are three points on level ground. Given that the bearing of R from P is 135 degrees, angle PQR = 55 degrees and angle PRQ = 48 degrees, find the bearing of. 6. A, B and C are three points on level ground. Given that the bearing of B from A is 122 degrees, angle CAB = 32 degrees and angle ABC = 86 degrees, find the possible bearing(s) of C from B.. 7. The figure shows four points on level ground. A is due north of D, B is due east of D and angle DBC = 37 degrees. Given AD = 34 m, AB = 57 m and BC = 28 m, find.

Worked Example: 1. The figure shows the positions of O, A, B, C and D. A is 33 degrees east of north, B is 28 degrees south of east, C is 44 degrees south of west, D is 39 degrees west of north. Find the bearing of: (i) A from O.

Formula used: Start at north, turn clockwise; convert quadrant descriptions from the nearest cardinal point; back bearing differs by 180.

Step 1: A is 33 degrees clockwise from north.

Answer: bearing of A from O = 033 degrees.

Worked Example: 1. (ii) B from O.

Formula used: Start at north, turn clockwise; convert quadrant descriptions from the nearest cardinal point; back bearing differs by 180.

Step 1: east is 090 degrees; B is 28 degrees further towards south.

Step 2: 90 + 28 = 118.

Answer: bearing of B from O = 118 degrees.

Worked Example: 2. The figure shows the position of P, A, B and C. A is 35 degrees north of east, B is 15 degrees east of south, C is 47 degrees north of west. Find the bearing of: (i) A from P.

Formula used: Start at north, turn clockwise; convert quadrant descriptions from the nearest cardinal point; back bearing differs by 180.

Step 1: east is 090 degrees; A is 35 degrees towards north, i.e. 35 degrees back.

Step 2: 90 - 35 = 55.

Answer: bearing of A from P = 055 degrees.

Worked Example: 2. (iv) P from A.

Formula used: Start at north, turn clockwise; convert quadrant descriptions from the nearest cardinal point; back bearing differs by 180.

Step 1: reverse bearing = forward bearing + 180 degrees.

Step 2: 55 + 180 = 235.

Answer: bearing of P from A = 235 degrees.

Worked Example: 4. A, B, C and D are the four corners of a rectangular plot marked out on level ground. Given that the bearing of B from A is 040 degrees and that the bearing of C from A is 090 degrees, find the bearing of: (i) B from C.

Formula used: Start at north, turn clockwise; convert quadrant descriptions from the nearest cardinal point; back bearing differs by 180.

Step 1: in rectangle ABCD, angle ABC = 90 degrees and angle BAC = 90 - 40 = 50 degrees, so angle BCA = 40 degrees.

Step 2: CA points west (270 degrees) from C; CB is 40 degrees towards north from CA.

Step 3: 270 + 40 = 310.

Answer: bearing of B from C = 310 degrees.

Worked Example: 6. A, B and C are three points on level ground. Given that the bearing of B from A is 122 degrees, angle CAB = 32 degrees and angle ABC = 86 degrees, find the possible bearing(s) of C from B.

Formula used: Start at north, turn clockwise; convert quadrant descriptions from the nearest cardinal point; back bearing differs by 180.

Step 1: bearing of A from B = 122 + 180 = 302 degrees.

Step 2: at B, C lies 86 degrees from BA on either side.

Step 3: 302 - 86 = 216 and 302 + 86 = 388 = 028.

Answer: the possible bearings of C from B are 216 degrees or 028 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point A is 33 degrees east of north from O. Find the bearing of A from O.
mcqs.why: Working: A is 33 degrees clockwise from north, and bearings use three figures, so the bearing is 033 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point B is 28 degrees south of east from O. Find the bearing of B from O.
mcqs.why: Working: east is 090 degrees and B is 28 degrees further towards south, so 90 + 28 = 118 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point C is 44 degrees south of west from O. Find the bearing of C from O.
mcqs.why: Working: the south-west quadrant starts at 180 degrees; C is 44 degrees south of west, so bearing = 270 - 44 = 226 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point D is 39 degrees west of north from O. Find the bearing of D from O.
mcqs.why: Working: west of north is before north on the clockwise scale, so bearing = 360 - 39 = 321 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point A is 35 degrees north of east from P. Find the bearing of A from P.
mcqs.why: Working: east is 090 degrees and A is 35 degrees towards north, i.e. back from east, so 90 - 35 = 55, written 055 degrees.

mcqs.q: The bearing of A from P is 055 degrees. Find the bearing of P from A.
mcqs.why: Working: back bearing = forward bearing + 180 degrees = 55 + 180 = 235 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point B is 15 degrees east of south from P. Find the bearing of B from P.
mcqs.why: Working: south is 180 degrees and B is 15 degrees towards east, i.e. back from south, so 180 - 15 = 165 degrees.

mcqs.q: Point C is 47 degrees north of west from P. Find the bearing of C from P.
mcqs.why: Working: west is 270 degrees and C is 47 degrees towards north, continuing clockwise, so 270 + 47 = 317 degrees.

mcqs.q: In a rectangular plot ABCD, the bearing of B from A is 040 degrees and the bearing of C from A is 090 degrees. Find the bearing of B from C.
mcqs.why: Working: angle BCA = 40 degrees; CA from C points west (270 degrees) and CB is 40 degrees towards north from CA, so 270 + 40 = 310 degrees.

mcqs.q: The bearing of B from A is 122 degrees. Find the bearing of A from B.
mcqs.why: Working: back bearing = forward bearing + 180 degrees = 122 + 180 = 302 degrees.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6 (pp.146-148)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 6: degree-radian conversion, the standard ratio values, elevation and depression problems, identity proofs, and bearings.

In this exercise: 1. Choose the correct options. 2. A person standing 30 m away from a tower has an eye level 1.5 m above the ground. The angle of elevation from his eyes to the top of the tower is 45 degrees. Determine the height of the tower.. 3. Prove that: sec^4 theta - tan^4 theta = 1 + 2 tan^2 theta.. 4. In figure, AD = 45 m, angle DAC = 30 degrees and angle DBC = 60 degrees and angle ACD = 90 degrees. Find. 5. Three points A, B and C lie on a horizontal ground. T is the top of the vertical tower standing on A. The bearings of B and C from A are 135 degrees and 225 degrees respectively and the bearing of C from B is 250 degrees. If BC = 50 m and angle of elevation of T from C is 35 degrees, calculate the angle of elevation of T from C. NOTE: the printed question repeats the given 35 degrees as its ask, so the notes give the quantities the data actually determine..

Worked Example: Q1. (i) 2pi/3 radian is equal to:

a) 140 degrees   b) 120 degrees   c) 100 degrees   d) 180 degrees

Answer: b) 120 degrees

Worked Example: Q1. (iv) If tan theta = 3/4, then sin theta =

a) 2/5   b) 3/5   c) 4/5   d) 1

Answer: b) 3/5

Worked Example: Q1. (vi) Bearings are written in figures:

a) two   b) three   c) four   d) five

Answer: b) three

Worked Example: 2. A person standing 30 m away from a tower has an eye level 1.5 m above the ground. The angle of elevation from his eyes to the top of the tower is 45 degrees. Determine the height of the tower.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 6 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: height above eye level = 30 x tan 45 degrees = 30 x 1 = 30 m.

Step 2: total height = 30 + 1.5.

Answer: height of the tower = 31.5 m.

Worked Example: 3. Prove that: sec^4 theta - tan^4 theta = 1 + 2 tan^2 theta.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 6 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: sec^4 theta - tan^4 theta = (sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta)(sec^2 theta + tan^2 theta).

Step 2: sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta = 1.

Step 3: sec^2 theta + tan^2 theta = (1 + tan^2 theta) + tan^2 theta = 1 + 2 tan^2 theta. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 4. In figure, AD = 45 m, angle DAC = 30 degrees and angle DBC = 60 degrees and angle ACD = 90 degrees. Find: (i) DC, (ii) AB, (iii) angle ADB.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 6 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: in right triangle ADC, DC = AD x sin 30 degrees = 45 x 0.5 = 22.5 m, and AC = AD x cos 30 degrees = 45 x √(3)/2 = 38.97 m.

Step 2: in right triangle DBC, BC = DC/tan 60 degrees = 22.5/√(3) = 12.99 m.

Step 3: AB = AC - BC = 38.97 - 12.99 = 25.98 m.

Step 4: angle ADC = 60 degrees and angle BDC = 30 degrees, so angle ADB = 60 - 30 = 30 degrees.

Answer: (i) DC = 22.5 m, (ii) AB = 25.98 m (approx), (iii) angle ADB = 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: 2pi/3 radians is equal to which angle?
mcqs.why: Working: degrees = (2pi/3) x (180/pi) = 2 x 180/3 = 120 degrees, pi cancels.

mcqs.q: If tan theta = 3/4, then sin theta is equal to what?
mcqs.why: Working: tan theta = 3/4 gives opposite 3, adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5, so sin theta = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

mcqs.q: Bearings are written in how many figures?
mcqs.why: Bearings are always written with three figures, for example 033 degrees and not 33 degrees.

mcqs.q: A person standing 30 m from a tower has eye level 1.5 m above the ground. The angle of elevation from his eyes to the top is 45 degrees. Find the height of the tower.
mcqs.why: Working: height above eye level = 30 x tan 45 degrees = 30 x 1 = 30 m; total height = 30 + 1.5 = 31.5 m.

mcqs.q: In a figure AD = 45 m, angle DAC = 30 degrees and angle ACD = 90 degrees. Find DC.
mcqs.why: Working: in right triangle ADC, DC = AD x sin 30 degrees = 45 x 0.5 = 22.5 m.

mcqs.q: In a figure AD = 45 m, angle DAC = 30 degrees and angle ACD = 90 degrees. Find AC.
mcqs.why: Working: in right triangle ADC, AC = AD x cos 30 degrees = 45 x sqrt(3)/2 = 45 x 0.8660 = 38.97 m approx.

mcqs.q: In a figure AD = 45 m, angle DAC = 30 degrees, angle DBC = 60 degrees and angle ACD = 90 degrees, with DC = 22.5 m and AC = 38.97 m. Find AB.
mcqs.why: Working: BC = DC / tan 60 degrees = 22.5 / sqrt(3) = 12.99 m; AB = AC - BC = 38.97 - 12.99 = 25.98 m approx.

mcqs.q: In a figure with angle DAC = 30 degrees and angle DBC = 60 degrees, angle ADC = 60 degrees and angle BDC = 30 degrees. Find angle ADB.
mcqs.why: Working: angle ADB = angle ADC - angle BDC = 60 - 30 = 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: In proving sec^4 theta - tan^4 theta = 1 + 2 tan^2 theta, the factor sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta is equal to what?
mcqs.why: Working: sec^4 - tan^4 = (sec^2 - tan^2)(sec^2 + tan^2) and sec^2 theta - tan^2 theta = 1 from 1 + tan^2 theta = sec^2 theta.

mcqs.q: Points A, B and C lie on horizontal ground. The bearings of B and C from A are 135 degrees and 225 degrees. Find the angle between AB and AC at A.
mcqs.why: Working: angle between the two bearings = 225 - 135 = 90 degrees.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Overview — Distance, Midpoint and Gradient
lessons.notes_html:
Every point of the plane is fixed by its coordinates (x, y): x measured along the horizontal axis, y along the vertical axis, from the origin O. Three formulas run the whole unit.

Formula: Distance PQ = sqrt( (x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 ).

Formula: Midpoint of PQ = ( (x1 + x2)/2 , (y1 + y2)/2 ).

Formula: Gradient (slope) m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).

Key Points

  • Collinear points: A, B, C are collinear if AB + BC = AC (distance test), or if the gradient of AB equals the gradient of BC (gradient test).
  • Triangles: two equal distances make an isosceles triangle; three equal distances an equilateral one; and if a^2 + b^2 = c^2 for the three squared distances, the triangle is right-angled (Pythagoras), the right angle opposite the longest side.
  • Quadrilaterals: a square has four equal sides and equal diagonals; a rectangle has equal opposite sides and equal diagonals.
  • The centre of a circle is the midpoint of any diameter.
  • Parallel lines have equal gradients: m1 = m2. Perpendicular lines have gradients whose product is -1: m1 x m2 = -1.

mcqs.q: What is the distance formula for the distance PQ between P(x1, y1) and Q(x2, y2)?
mcqs.why: The horizontal change x2 - x1 and vertical change y2 - y1 are squared, added, and then the square root is taken.

mcqs.q: What is the midpoint of the segment joining P(x1, y1) and Q(x2, y2)?
mcqs.why: The midpoint is found by averaging the two x-coordinates and averaging the two y-coordinates separately.

mcqs.q: What is the gradient m of the line through P(x1, y1) and Q(x2, y2)?
mcqs.why: Gradient is the change in y divided by the corresponding change in x, keeping the same point order top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Using distances, when are three points A, B and C collinear?
mcqs.why: Points are collinear by the distance test when the two shorter distances add up exactly to the longest distance AC.

mcqs.q: When are two lines parallel?
mcqs.why: Parallel lines have the same steepness, so their gradients are equal: the parallel test is m1 = m2.

mcqs.q: When are two lines perpendicular?
mcqs.why: Perpendicular lines have gradients whose product is -1, which is the perpendicular test m1 x m2 = -1.

mcqs.q: The centre of a circle whose diameter has endpoints P and Q is which point?
options: A point at distance PQ from P
mcqs.why: The centre of a circle is the midpoint of any diameter, so it is the midpoint of the segment PQ.

mcqs.q: Which distance properties describe a square?
options: Only one pair of equal sides
Four equal sides and unequal diagonals
Four equal sides and equal diagonals
mcqs.why: A square has all four sides equal and its two diagonals are also equal, as stated in the key points.

mcqs.q: Which distance properties describe a rectangle?
options: All four sides equal and unequal diagonals
Equal opposite sides and equal diagonals
Only the diagonals are equal, with no equal sides
mcqs.why: A rectangle has equal opposite sides and equal diagonals; it does not require all four sides to be equal.

mcqs.q: If the squared distances of a triangle satisfy a^2 + b^2 = c^2, what is the triangle?
options: Right-angled, with the right angle opposite the longest side
mcqs.why: By Pythagoras, a^2 + b^2 = c^2 for the squared distances means a right angle, opposite the longest side c.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 (p.160) - Distance and Midpoint
lessons.notes_html:
The distance formula is Pythagoras in coordinates: the horizontal change (x2 - x1) and the vertical change (y2 - y1) are the two sides of a right-angled triangle, and the distance is its hypotenuse. Square carefully with negative coordinates — a minus times a minus is a plus.

Shape proofs are distance calculations in disguise: compute the three (or four) squared distances and compare them — equal sides, Pythagoras for a right angle, equal diagonals for a rectangle or square. The midpoint is the average of the two x-values and the average of the two y-values; it is also the centre of a circle when the segment is a diameter.

Formula: d = sqrt( (x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 ) ; Midpoint = ( (x1 + x2)/2 , (y1 + y2)/2 )

In this exercise: 1. Find distance between the following points. 2. Show that whether A(1, -1), B(2, 2) and C(4, 3) are collinear or not.. 3. If two vertices of an equilateral triangle are A(-3, 0) and B(3, 0), find the third vertex.. 4. Show that the points P(-2, 8), Q(3, 20) and (11, 8) are the vertices of an isosceles triangle.. 5. Show that the points A(0, 2), B(√(3), -1) and C(0, -2) are the vertices of a right angled triangle.. 6. Show that the points A(5, 2), B(-2, 3), C(-3, -4) and D(4, -5) are the vertices of the square.. 7. Show that P(0, 7), Q(6, 5), R(5, 2) and S(-1, 4) are the vertices of a rectangle.. 8. Find the coordinates of the midpoint of the line segment joining the following pair of points. 9. A(-2, 1) and B(6, 5) are opposite ends of the diameter of a circle. Find coordinates of its midpoint.. 10. The coordinate of the midpoint of the line joining A(p^2, p) and B(-q^2, q) are (5, 1). Find the possible values of p and q.. 11. Find the value of P so that (-2, 2.5) is the midpoint between (P, 2) and (-1, 3)..

Worked Example: 1. Find distance between the following points: (i) (2, 5) and (5, 10).

Formula used: Distance: square both changes, add, take the square root. Midpoint: average the x-values and average the y-values.

Step 1: d = √((5 - 2)^2 + (10 - 5)^2).

Step 2: d = √(9 + 25).

Answer: d = √(34) units.

Worked Example: 2. Show that whether A(1, -1), B(2, 2) and C(4, 3) are collinear or not.

Formula used: Distance: square both changes, add, take the square root. Midpoint: average the x-values and average the y-values.

Step 1: AB = √(1 + 9) = √(10); BC = √(4 + 1) = √(5); AC = √(9 + 16) = 5.

Step 2: √(10) + √(5) = 5.40 (approx), which is not equal to 5, and no other sum of two sides equals the third.

Answer: the points are NOT collinear.

Worked Example: 3. If two vertices of an equilateral triangle are A(-3, 0) and B(3, 0), find the third vertex.

Formula used: Distance: square both changes, add, take the square root. Midpoint: average the x-values and average the y-values.

Step 1: AB = 6 units, so the third vertex lies on the perpendicular bisector x = 0.

Step 2: height = (6 x √(3))/2 = 3 x √(3).

Answer: the third vertex is (0, 3 x √(3)) or (0, -3 x √(3)).

Worked Example: 5. Show that the points A(0, 2), B(√(3), -1) and C(0, -2) are the vertices of a right angled triangle.

Formula used: Distance: square both changes, add, take the square root. Midpoint: average the x-values and average the y-values.

Step 1: AB^2 = 3 + 9 = 12; BC^2 = 3 + 1 = 4; AC^2 = 0 + 16 = 16.

Step 2: AB^2 + BC^2 = 12 + 4 = 16 = AC^2.

Answer: by Pythagoras, the triangle is right angled at B.

Worked Example: 8. Find the coordinates of the midpoint of the line segment joining the following pair of points: (i) (6, 7) and (4, 3).

Formula used: Distance: square both changes, add, take the square root. Midpoint: average the x-values and average the y-values.

Step 1: x = (6 + 4)/2 = 5.

Step 2: y = (7 + 3)/2 = 5.

Answer: midpoint = (5, 5).

Worked Example: 9. A(-2, 1) and B(6, 5) are opposite ends of the diameter of a circle. Find coordinates of its midpoint.

Formula used: Distance: square both changes, add, take the square root. Midpoint: average the x-values and average the y-values.

Step 1: the centre is the midpoint of the diameter.

Step 2: x = (-2 + 6)/2 = 2; y = (1 + 5)/2 = 3.

Answer: midpoint (centre) = (2, 3).

mcqs.q: Find the distance between (2, 5) and (5, 10).
mcqs.why: Distance = sqrt((5 - 2)^2 + (10 - 5)^2) = sqrt(9 + 25) = sqrt(34) units.

mcqs.q: Are A(1, -1), B(2, 2) and C(4, 3) collinear?
options: B is the midpoint of AC
A is the midpoint of BC
mcqs.why: AB = sqrt(10), BC = sqrt(5) and AC = 5; sqrt(10) + sqrt(5) is about 5.40, not 5, so AB + BC is not AC.

mcqs.q: Two vertices of an equilateral triangle are A(-3, 0) and B(3, 0). Which point can be the third vertex?
mcqs.why: AB = 6, so the third vertex is on x = 0 at height (6 x sqrt(3))/2 = 3 sqrt(3), giving (0, 3 sqrt(3)).

mcqs.q: For A(0, 2), B(sqrt(3), -1) and C(0, -2), the triangle is right-angled at which vertex?
mcqs.why: AB^2 = 3 + 9 = 12, BC^2 = 3 + 1 = 4 and AC^2 = 16; 12 + 4 = 16, so by Pythagoras the right angle is at B.

mcqs.q: Find the midpoint of the segment joining (6, 7) and (4, 3).
A(-2, 1) and B(6, 5) are opposite ends of a diameter. What is the centre of the circle?
mcqs.why: The centre is the midpoint of the diameter: ((-2 + 6)/2, (1 + 5)/2) = (4/2, 6/2) = (2, 3).

mcqs.q: Find the value of P so that (-2, 2.5) is the midpoint of (P, 2) and (-1, 3).
mcqs.why: For the x-coordinate, (P + (-1))/2 = -2, so P - 1 = -4 and therefore P = -3; the y-check is (2 + 3)/2 = 2.5.

mcqs.q: The midpoint of A(p^2, p) and B(-q^2, q) is (5, 1). What is p + q?
mcqs.why: For the y-coordinate, (p + q)/2 = 1, and multiplying both sides by 2 gives p + q = 2.

mcqs.q: What shape is formed by A(5, 2), B(-2, 3), C(-3, -4) and D(4, -5)?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
mcqs.why: AB^2 = 49 + 1 = 50, BC^2 = 1 + 49 = 50, CD^2 = 50 and DA^2 = 50, so all sides are equal; diagonals AC^2 = 64 + 36 = 100 and BD^2 = 36 + 64 = 100 are also equal, the test for a square.

mcqs.q: P(-2, 8), Q(3, 20) and R(11, 8) form an isosceles triangle. Which two sides are equal?
mcqs.why: PQ = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = 13 and PR = sqrt(13^2 + 0^2) = 13, while QR = sqrt(208), so PQ = PR and the triangle is isosceles.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.2 (pp.168-169) - Gradient, Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
lessons.notes_html:
The gradient m = (change in y) / (change in x) measures the steepness of the line through two points; keep the same point order top and bottom. A positive gradient rises to the right, a negative gradient falls. Two lines are parallel when their gradients are equal, and perpendicular when the product of their gradients is -1.

For collinear points, set the gradients of the two segments equal and solve for the unknown. Q5 shows that sometimes no value of the unknown works — the honest answer is then "no such value", with the reason shown.

Formula: m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) ; parallel: m1 = m2 ; perpendicular: m1 x m2 = -1

In this exercise: 1. Find the gradient of the line passing through each of the following pairs of points. 2. If the gradient of a line joining the points (k, -5) and (2, -4k) is -4, find the value of k.. 3. Check whether the following pairs of points joining the line are parallel, perpendicular or neither. 4. The points A(2, -3), B(3, -2) and C(8, z) are collinear, find the value of z.. 5. The co-ordinates of four points O(0, 0), P(2, 1), Q(3, 9) and R(3h, 2h + 7). Find the value(s) of h if. 6. Two airports are located on a straight line where A(4, 5) and B(10, 13). What is the distance between the airports?. 7. A city park is located at a point (4, 7) on a map. A library is located at (12, 15). What is the distance between the city park and the library? Additionally, what is the midpoint of the park and the library?. 8. The school is located at (5, 8) and a student's home is at (11, 12). How far is the student's home from the school and what is the midpoint of his route?. 9. A new road is being constructed between town A(3, 4) and B(9, 14). The engineer needs to determine the gradient of the road. What is the gradient of the road between town A and B?.

Worked Example: 1. Find the gradient of the line passing through each of the following pairs of points: (i) A(0, 0), B(-5, 2).

Formula used: Gradient = rise over run; equal gradients = parallel; product of gradients = -1 = perpendicular; equal gradients through a common point = collinear.

Step 1: m = (2 - 0)/(-5 - 0) = 2/(-5).

Answer: m = -2/5.

Worked Example: 2. If the gradient of a line joining the points (k, -5) and (2, -4k) is -4, find the value of k.

Formula used: Gradient = rise over run; equal gradients = parallel; product of gradients = -1 = perpendicular; equal gradients through a common point = collinear.

Step 1: (-4k + 5)/(2 - k) = -4.

Step 2: -4k + 5 = -8 + 4k.

Step 3: 13 = 8k.

Answer: k = 13/8.

Worked Example: 3. Check whether the following pairs of points joining the line are parallel, perpendicular or neither: (i) (5, 7), (7, 8) and (7, -5), (19, 1).

Formula used: Gradient = rise over run; equal gradients = parallel; product of gradients = -1 = perpendicular; equal gradients through a common point = collinear.

Step 1: m1 = (8 - 7)/(7 - 5) = 1/2.

Step 2: m2 = (1 + 5)/(19 - 7) = 6/12 = 1/2.

Step 3: m1 = m2.

Answer: the lines are parallel.

Worked Example: 3. (iii) (3, 7), (-6, 9) and (3, 18), (5, 27).

Formula used: Gradient = rise over run; equal gradients = parallel; product of gradients = -1 = perpendicular; equal gradients through a common point = collinear.

Step 1: m1 = (9 - 7)/(-6 - 3) = -2/9.

Step 2: m2 = (27 - 18)/(5 - 3) = 9/2.

Step 3: m1 x m2 = -1.

Answer: the lines are perpendicular.

Worked Example: 4. The points A(2, -3), B(3, -2) and C(8, z) are collinear, find the value of z.

Formula used: Gradient = rise over run; equal gradients = parallel; product of gradients = -1 = perpendicular; equal gradients through a common point = collinear.

Step 1: slope of AB = (-2 + 3)/(3 - 2) = 1.

Step 2: slope of BC = (z + 2)/(8 - 3) = (z + 2)/5.

Step 3: for collinearity (z + 2)/5 = 1, so z + 2 = 5.

Answer: z = 3.

Worked Example: 6. Two airports are located on a straight line where A(4, 5) and B(10, 13). What is the distance between the airports?

Formula used: Gradient = rise over run; equal gradients = parallel; product of gradients = -1 = perpendicular; equal gradients through a common point = collinear.

Step 1: d = √((10 - 4)^2 + (13 - 5)^2) = √(36 + 64).

Answer: d = 10 units.

mcqs.q: Find the gradient of the line through A(0, 0) and B(-5, 2).
mcqs.why: Gradient m = (2 - 0)/(-5 - 0) = 2/(-5) = -2/5, using the same point order top and bottom.

mcqs.q: If the gradient of the line joining (k, -5) and (2, -4k) is -4, find k.
The lines through (5, 7), (7, 8) and through (7, -5), (19, 1) are:
mcqs.why: m1 = (8 - 7)/(7 - 5) = 1/2 and m2 = (1 + 5)/(19 - 7) = 6/12 = 1/2; equal gradients mean the lines are parallel.

mcqs.q: The lines through (3, 7), (-6, 9) and through (3, 18), (5, 27) are:
mcqs.why: m1 = (9 - 7)/(-6 - 3) = -2/9 and m2 = (27 - 18)/(5 - 3) = 9/2; their product is -1, so the lines are perpendicular.

mcqs.q: A(2, -3), B(3, -2) and C(8, z) are collinear. Find z.
mcqs.why: Slope AB = (-2 + 3)/(3 - 2) = 1; slope BC = (z + 2)/5; setting (z + 2)/5 = 1 gives z + 2 = 5, so z = 3.

mcqs.q: Two airports are at A(4, 5) and B(10, 13). What is the distance between them?
A park is at (4, 7) and a library is at (12, 15). What is the distance between them?
mcqs.why: Distance = sqrt((12 - 4)^2 + (15 - 7)^2) = sqrt(64 + 64) = sqrt(128) units.

mcqs.q: A park is at (4, 7) and a library is at (12, 15). What is their midpoint?
A school is at (5, 8) and a home is at (11, 12). What is the distance between them?
mcqs.why: Distance = sqrt((11 - 5)^2 + (12 - 8)^2) = sqrt(36 + 16) = sqrt(52) units.

mcqs.q: Find the gradient of the road between town A(3, 4) and town B(9, 14).
mcqs.why: Gradient m = (14 - 4)/(9 - 3) = 10/6 = 5/3, which is the rise divided by the run.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 7 (p.169)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 7: distance, midpoint, gradient, and the parallel/perpendicular tests. Note Q4: as printed, the book asks to show two lines are perpendicular, but their gradients 3/4 and 4/3 have product +1, not -1 — the lines are NOT perpendicular, and the notes say so plainly instead of faking the proof.

In this exercise: 1. Choose the correct options. 2. Find the gradient of the following points joining the line. 3. Show that the points A(1, 2), B(3, 6) and (5, 10) are collinear.. 4. Show that the points joining the lines A(3, 5), B(7, 8) and C(5, 8), D(8, 12) are perpendicular. NOTE: as printed this claim does NOT hold — the working below proves the opposite, and the notes do not fake the proof.. 5. Two locations in a park are located at points P(2, 3) and Q(10, 7). What is the midpoint and distance between them?.

Worked Example: Q1. (i) Distance between A(4, 5) and B(1, 9) is:

a) 2.5   b) 5   c) 7.5   d) 10

Answer: b) 5

Worked Example: Q1. (iv) If m1 x m2 = -1 then the lines are:

a) parallel   b) intersecting   c) perpendicular   d) none of these

Answer: c) perpendicular

Worked Example: 2. Find the gradient of the following points joining the line: (i) A(-6, 0), B(-4, 5).

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 7 Overview and Lessons 1 and 2 of this unit.

Step 1: m = (5 - 0)/(-4 + 6) = 5/2.

Answer: m = 5/2.

Worked Example: 3. Show that the points A(1, 2), B(3, 6) and (5, 10) are collinear.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 7 Overview and Lessons 1 and 2 of this unit.

Step 1: slope of AB = (6 - 2)/(3 - 1) = 2.

Step 2: slope of the second pair = (10 - 6)/(5 - 3) = 2.

Step 3: equal slopes with B common.

Answer: the points are collinear.

Worked Example: 4. Show that the points joining the lines A(3, 5), B(7, 8) and C(5, 8), D(8, 12) are perpendicular. NOTE: as printed this claim does NOT hold — the working below proves the opposite, and the notes do not fake the proof.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 7 Overview and Lessons 1 and 2 of this unit.

Step 1: slope of AB = (8 - 5)/(7 - 3) = 3/4.

Step 2: slope of CD = (12 - 8)/(8 - 5) = 4/3.

Step 3: (3/4) x (4/3) = 1, not -1. Answer: the lines are NOT perpendicular as printed (their slopes are reciprocals with product +1); the book's statement is an error.

mcqs.q: What is the distance between A(4, 5) and B(1, 9)?
If m1 x m2 = -1, then the two lines are:
mcqs.why: The product of the gradients being -1 is exactly the perpendicular test, so the lines are perpendicular.

mcqs.q: Find the gradient of the line joining A(-6, 0) and B(-4, 5).
mcqs.why: Gradient m = (5 - 0)/(-4 - (-6)) = 5/2, because the x-change is -4 + 6 = 2.

mcqs.q: Are A(1, 2), B(3, 6) and C(5, 10) collinear?
options: No, the points are not collinear
Only A and B are on the line
mcqs.why: Slope AB = (6 - 2)/(3 - 1) = 2 and slope BC = (10 - 6)/(5 - 3) = 2; equal slopes through the common point B mean collinearity.

mcqs.q: For the lines through A(3, 5), B(7, 8) and through C(5, 8), D(8, 12), what is the correct conclusion?
mcqs.why: Slope AB = 3/4 and slope CD = 4/3; their product is (3/4) x (4/3) = +1, not -1, so the lines are NOT perpendicular.

mcqs.q: Two locations in a park are P(2, 3) and Q(10, 7). What is their midpoint?
Two locations in a park are P(2, 3) and Q(10, 7). What is the distance between them?
mcqs.why: Distance = sqrt((10 - 2)^2 + (7 - 3)^2) = sqrt(64 + 16) = sqrt(80) units.

mcqs.q: What is the gradient of the line joining A(1, 2) and B(3, 6)?
mcqs.why: Gradient m = (6 - 2)/(3 - 1) = 4/2 = 2, calculated directly from the two points given.

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line through C(5, 8) and D(8, 12)?
mcqs.why: Slope = (12 - 8)/(8 - 5) = 4/3, which is the slope of CD used in Review Exercise 7 Question 4.

mcqs.q: What is the midpoint of A(1, 2) and C(5, 10)?
mcqs.why: Midpoint = ((1 + 5)/2, (2 + 10)/2) = (6/2, 12/2) = (3, 6), which is the point B in the collinearity example.

lessons.title: Unit 8 Overview — Equations of a Straight Line
lessons.notes_html:
A straight line is fixed by its slope m and one point on it. The slope is the tangent of the angle the line makes with the positive x-axis: m = tan theta = rise / run.

Formula: Slope-intercept form: y = mx + c (c = the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis).

Formula: Point-slope form: y - y1 = m (x - x1) for the line of slope m through (x1, y1).

Key Points

  • Two-point form: first find m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1), then use the point-slope form with either point.
  • Intercept form: x/a + y/b = 1, where a and b are the x- and y-intercepts. Equal intercepts means a = b.
  • Normal form: x cos alpha + y sin alpha = p, where p is the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line. To reduce ax + by + c = 0 to normal form, divide every term by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) (sign chosen so p is positive).
  • Symmetric form: (x - x1)/cos alpha = (y - y1)/sin alpha = r, where r is the distance along the line from (x1, y1).
  • From the general form ax + by + c = 0, the slope is m = -a/b and the perpendicular distance from the origin is |c| / sqrt(a^2 + b^2).
  • Angle between two lines of slopes m1 and m2: tan theta = | (m2 - m1) / (1 + m1 m2) |. In coefficient form the angle from a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 to a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 is tan^-1( (a1b2 - a2b1) / (a1a2 + b1b2) ); the lines are parallel when a1b2 - a2b1 = 0 and perpendicular when a1a2 + b1b2 = 0.
  • For the interior angles of a triangle, find the three side slopes, take the angle between each pair, and convert an obtuse supplement where the interior angle is the one inside the triangle; the three must add to 180 degrees.
  • A line through a point of intersection: solve the two given lines simultaneously to find the point, then use the two-point method.

mcqs.q: In the slope-intercept form y = mx + c, what does c represent?
options: The y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis
mcqs.why: In y = mx + c, m is the slope and c is the y-intercept, the point where the line crosses the y-axis.

mcqs.q: What is the point-slope form for a line of slope m through (x1, y1)?
options: x cos alpha + y sin alpha = p
mcqs.why: The point-slope form uses the given slope and one point: y - y1 = m(x - x1).

mcqs.q: What is the intercept form of a straight line?
options: x cos alpha + y sin alpha = p
mcqs.why: The intercept form is x/a + y/b = 1, where a is the x-intercept and b is the y-intercept.

mcqs.q: In the normal form x cos alpha + y sin alpha = p, what is p?
options: The perpendicular distance from the origin to the line
mcqs.why: In normal form, p is defined as the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line, and p is taken positive.

mcqs.q: From the general form ax + by + c = 0, what is the slope m?
mcqs.why: Rearranging ax + by + c = 0 gives by = -ax - c, so the slope is m = -a/b.

mcqs.q: From ax + by + c = 0, what is the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line?
mcqs.why: The overview gives the perpendicular distance from the origin as |c| divided by sqrt(a^2 + b^2).

mcqs.q: What is the formula for tan theta, the angle between lines of slopes m1 and m2?
mcqs.why: The angle between two lines satisfies tan theta = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2)|, with the absolute value giving the acute angle.

mcqs.q: For lines a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0, when are they parallel?
mcqs.why: In coefficient form the lines are parallel when the numerator a1b2 - a2b1 is zero, making the angle zero.

mcqs.q: For lines a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0, when are they perpendicular?
mcqs.why: In coefficient form the lines are perpendicular when the denominator a1a2 + b1b2 is zero.

mcqs.q: The slope m of a line is related to the angle theta it makes with the positive x-axis by:
mcqs.why: The overview defines the slope as the tangent of the angle with the positive x-axis: m = tan theta = rise/run.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.1 (p.179) - Finding the Equation of a Line
lessons.notes_html:
Every question here is one of three recipes: (1) slope and intercept given — write y = mx + c at once (if a point is given instead of c, substitute the point to find c); (2) slope and a point given — use the point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); (3) two points given — find the slope first, then recipe (2).

Special cases: a line making an angle theta with the x-axis has slope m = tan theta; a perpendicular line has slope the negative reciprocal of the given slope; a line with equal intercepts uses x/a + y/a = 1.

Formula: y = mx + c ; y - y1 = m(x - x1) ; m = tan theta

In this exercise: 1. Find the equation of straight line using slope-intercept form if it has. 2. Find the equation of straight line using point-slope form if it has. 3. Find the equation of the line passing through (7, 11) and perpendicular to a line through (-1, 5) and (7, 6).. 4. Find the equation of line passing through (3, -2) making an angle 135 degrees with x-axis.. 5. Find equation of line passing two points. 6. Find the equation of the line passing through (8, 3) and also passing the midpoint of the line segment joining (3, 5) and (8, 10).. 7. Find the equation of the line passing through (-8, -1) and making equal intercepts on the coordinate axes.. 8. A line makes the positive intercepts on coordinate axes whose sum is 9 and passes through (-3, 5), then find the equation of the straight line..

Worked Example: 1. Find the equation of straight line using slope-intercept form if it has: (i) gradient 7 and y-intercept -8.

Formula used: Point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); find m from two points, from tan theta, or as the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

Step 1: y = mx + c with m = 7 and c = -8.

Answer: y = 7x - 8.

Worked Example: 2. Find the equation of straight line using point-slope form if it has: (i) slope -3 and passing through (7, 3).

Formula used: Point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); find m from two points, from tan theta, or as the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

Step 1: y - 3 = -3(x - 7).

Step 2: y - 3 = -3x + 21.

Answer: 3x + y - 24 = 0.

Worked Example: 3. Find the equation of the line passing through (7, 11) and perpendicular to a line through (-1, 5) and (7, 6).

Formula used: Point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); find m from two points, from tan theta, or as the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

Step 1: slope of the given line = (6 - 5)/(7 + 1) = 1/8.

Step 2: slope of the required line = -8 (negative reciprocal).

Step 3: y - 11 = -8(x - 7).

Answer: 8x + y - 67 = 0.

Worked Example: 5. Find equation of line passing two points: (i) (-1, 5) and (2, 8).

Formula used: Point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); find m from two points, from tan theta, or as the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

Step 1: slope = (8 - 5)/(2 + 1) = 1.

Step 2: y - 5 = 1(x + 1).

Answer: x - y + 6 = 0.

Worked Example: 6. Find the equation of the line passing through (8, 3) and also passing the midpoint of the line segment joining (3, 5) and (8, 10).

Formula used: Point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); find m from two points, from tan theta, or as the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

Step 1: midpoint = ((3 + 8)/2, (5 + 10)/2) = (11/2, 15/2).

Step 2: slope = (15/2 - 3)/(11/2 - 8) = (9/2)/(-5/2) = -9/5.

Step 3: y - 3 = (-9/5)(x - 8).

Answer: 9x + 5y - 87 = 0.

Worked Example: 7. Find the equation of the line passing through (-8, -1) and making equal intercepts on the coordinate axes.

Formula used: Point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1); find m from two points, from tan theta, or as the negative reciprocal for a perpendicular line.

Step 1: with equal intercepts a, x/a + y/a = 1, i.e. x + y = a.

Step 2: -8 + (-1) = a, so a = -9.

Answer: x + y + 9 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 7 and y-intercept -8.
mcqs.why: Use y = mx + c with m = 7 and c = -8, which gives y = 7x - 8 directly.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line with slope -3 passing through (7, 3).
mcqs.why: Point-slope: y - 3 = -3(x - 7), so y - 3 = -3x + 21 and rearranged this is 3x + y - 24 = 0; check: 21 + 3 - 24 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line through (7, 11) perpendicular to the line through (-1, 5) and (7, 6).
mcqs.why: Given slope = (6 - 5)/(7 + 1) = 1/8, so the perpendicular slope is -8; y - 11 = -8(x - 7) gives 8x + y - 67 = 0; check: 56 + 11 - 67 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line through (3, -2) making an angle of 135 degrees with the x-axis.
mcqs.why: Slope m = tan 135 degrees = -1; y + 2 = -1(x - 3) gives x + y - 1 = 0; check: 3 + (-2) - 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line passing through (-1, 5) and (2, 8).
Find the equation of the line through (8, 3) and the midpoint of the segment joining (3, 5) and (8, 10).
Find the equation of the line through (-8, -1) making equal intercepts on the axes.
mcqs.why: With equal intercepts a, x/a + y/a = 1 gives x + y = a; substituting (-8, -1) gives a = -9, so the line is x + y + 9 = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the midpoint of the segment joining (3, 5) and (8, 10)?
mcqs.why: Midpoint = ((3 + 8)/2, (5 + 10)/2) = (11/2, 15/2), the second point used in Exercise 8.1 Question 6.

mcqs.q: The line through (-1, 5) and (7, 6) has slope 1/8. What is the slope of a line perpendicular to it?
mcqs.why: A perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of 1/8, which is -8, because (1/8) x (-8) = -1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 5 and y-intercept 3.
mcqs.why: Use the slope-intercept form y = mx + c with m = 5 and c = 3, giving y = 5x + 3 at once.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.2 (pp.185-186) - Reducing an Equation to Standard Forms
lessons.notes_html:
To reduce ax + by + c = 0: for slope-intercept form, make y the subject; for intercept form, move the constant to the right, divide so the right side is 1, and read off a and b; for normal form, divide every term by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) so the coefficients of x and y become cos alpha and sin alpha and the constant becomes p, the perpendicular distance from the origin.

The last questions are the same mathematics in real settings — depreciation of a machine, the Celsius-Fahrenheit line, a filling water tank, and a road through two towns (a third point lies on the road exactly when it satisfies the equation).

Formula: x/a + y/b = 1 ; x cos alpha + y sin alpha = p ; divide by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) for normal form

In this exercise: 1. Reduce the equation 3x - 8y = 24 to the. 2. Reduce the equation 3x + 5y = 15 to the. 3. If P is the perpendicular distance from the origin to a line whose intercepts on the axes are a and b, show that: 1/P^2 = 1/a^2 + 1/b^2.. 4. Three villages A, B and C are connected by straight roads with vertices (3, 5), (9, 7) and (-3, 5) respectively. Find. 5. The value of a machine is expected to decrease: its value 1 year after the date of purchase will be Rs.90,000 and its value after 5 years is expected to be Rs.60,000.. 6. If C represents temperature in degrees Celsius and F represents temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, assume that the relationship between the two scales is linear and is graphed with F on vertical axis. Two temperature pairs on this line are (5, 41) and (25, 77). Using these points, find the equation of the straight line (in the form C = mF + K). Also, explain the meaning of slope, the C-intercept and F-intercept.. 7. A water tank is being filled at a constant rate. After 2 hours, the water level reaches 150 litres, and the filling rate is 30 litres per hour. Write the equation of water level y (in litres) after x hours and find the water after 5 hours.. 8. A straight road passes through two towns, A(2, 3) and B(8, 9) on a coordinate map. Find the equation of the road and also check whether a third town C(5, 6) lies on the same road..

Worked Example: 1. Reduce the equation 3x - 8y = 24 to the: (i) slope-intercept form, (ii) intercepts form, (iii) normal form.

Formula used: Make y the subject (slope-intercept); divide to make the constant 1 (intercepts); divide by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) (normal form).

Step 1: (i) 8y = 3x - 24, so y = (3/8)x - 3.

Step 2: (ii) dividing by 24: x/8 + y/(-3) = 1.

Step 3: (iii) dividing by √(9 + 64) = √(73): (3/√(73))x - (8/√(73))y = 24/√(73), i.e. x cos alpha + y sin alpha = p with cos alpha = 3/√(73), sin alpha = -8/√(73), p = 24/√(73).

Answer: (i) y = (3/8)x - 3; (ii) x/8 - y/3 = 1; (iii) (3x - 8y)/√(73) = 24/√(73).

Worked Example: 2. Reduce the equation 3x + 5y = 15 to the: (i) slope-intercept form, (ii) intercepts form, (iii) symmetric form, (iv) normal form.

Formula used: Make y the subject (slope-intercept); divide to make the constant 1 (intercepts); divide by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) (normal form).

Step 1: (i) 5y = -3x + 15, so y = (-3/5)x + 3.

Step 2: (ii) dividing by 15: x/5 + y/3 = 1.

Step 3: (iii) the x-intercept is (5, 0) and slope = -3/5 = tan alpha, so cos alpha = 5/√(34) and sin alpha = -3/√(34); symmetric form: (x - 5)/(5/√(34)) = y/(-3/√(34)).

Step 4: (iv) dividing by √(34): (3/√(34))x + (5/√(34))y = 15/√(34).

Answer: (i) y = (-3/5)x + 3; (ii) x/5 + y/3 = 1; (iii) (x - 5)/(5/√(34)) = y/(-3/√(34)); (iv) (3x + 5y)/√(34) = 15/√(34).

Worked Example: 3. If P is the perpendicular distance from the origin to a line whose intercepts on the axes are a and b, show that: 1/P^2 = 1/a^2 + 1/b^2.

Formula used: Make y the subject (slope-intercept); divide to make the constant 1 (intercepts); divide by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) (normal form).

Step 1: the line is x/a + y/b = 1, i.e. (1/a)x + (1/b)y - 1 = 0.

Step 2: distance from the origin P = | -1 |/√((1/a)^2 + (1/b)^2) = 1/√(1/a^2 + 1/b^2).

Step 3: squaring and taking reciprocals: 1/P^2 = 1/a^2 + 1/b^2. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 5. The value of a machine is expected to decrease: its value 1 year after the date of purchase will be Rs.90,000 and its value after 5 years is expected to be Rs.60,000. (i) Determine the slope intercept equation (V = mt + K) which relates the value V of the machine to its age t, stated in years. (ii) Interpret the meaning of the slope and V intercept. (iii) Determine the t-intercept and interpret the meaning.

Formula used: Make y the subject (slope-intercept); divide to make the constant 1 (intercepts); divide by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) (normal form).

Step 1: (i) slope m = (60000 - 90000)/(5 - 1) = -7500.

Step 2: V = -7500t + K and 90000 = -7500 + K, so K = 97500. Answer: (i) V = -7500t + 97500.

Step 3: (ii) the slope -7500 means the machine loses Rs.7,500 of value per year; the V-intercept 97500 is the value at purchase (t = 0).

Step 4: (iii) V = 0 gives t = 97500/7500 = 13.

Answer: t-intercept = 13 years, i.e. the machine's value reaches zero after 13 years.

Worked Example: 8. A straight road passes through two towns, A(2, 3) and B(8, 9) on a coordinate map. Find the equation of the road and also check whether a third town C(5, 6) lies on the same road.

Formula used: Make y the subject (slope-intercept); divide to make the constant 1 (intercepts); divide by sqrt(a^2 + b^2) (normal form).

Step 1: slope = (9 - 3)/(8 - 2) = 1.

Step 2: y - 3 = 1(x - 2), i.e. x - y + 1 = 0.

Step 3: for C(5, 6): 5 - 6 + 1 = 0.

Answer: equation x - y + 1 = 0; C(5, 6) DOES lie on the same road.

mcqs.q: Reduce 3x - 8y = 24 to slope-intercept form.
mcqs.why: Make y the subject: 8y = 3x - 24, so dividing by 8 gives y = (3/8)x - 3.

mcqs.q: Reduce 3x - 8y = 24 to intercept form.
mcqs.why: Divide by 24: x/8 + y/(-3) = 1, which is written x/8 - y/3 = 1, so the intercepts are 8 and -3.

mcqs.q: When 3x - 8y = 24 is reduced to normal form, what is p, the distance from the origin?
mcqs.why: Divide by sqrt(3^2 + (-8)^2) = sqrt(73); the constant becomes p = 24/sqrt(73) in (3x - 8y)/sqrt(73) = 24/sqrt(73).

mcqs.q: Reduce 3x + 5y = 15 to slope-intercept form.
mcqs.why: Make y the subject: 5y = -3x + 15, so dividing by 5 gives y = (-3/5)x + 3.

mcqs.q: Reduce 3x + 5y = 15 to intercept form.
mcqs.why: Divide every term by 15: x/5 + y/3 = 1, so the x-intercept is 5 and the y-intercept is 3.

mcqs.q: When 3x + 5y = 15 is reduced to normal form, what is p?
mcqs.why: Divide by sqrt(3^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(34); the constant becomes p = 15/sqrt(34) in (3x + 5y)/sqrt(34) = 15/sqrt(34).

mcqs.q: A machine is worth Rs.90,000 after 1 year and Rs.60,000 after 5 years. What is its value equation V in terms of age t?
For the machine V = -7500t + 97500, what is the t-intercept and its meaning?
options: 10 years, when the value reaches zero
13 years, when the value reaches zero
7.5 years, when the value reaches zero
mcqs.why: Set V = 0: 0 = -7500t + 97500, so t = 97500/7500 = 13; after 13 years the machine value reaches zero.

mcqs.q: A road passes through A(2, 3) and B(8, 9). What is the equation of the road?
A tank is filled at 30 litres per hour and holds 150 litres after 2 hours. How much water is in it after 5 hours?
mcqs.why: Level y = 30x + K and 150 = 30(2) + K gives K = 90, so y = 30x + 90; at x = 5, y = 150 + 90 = 240 litres.

lessons.title: Exercise 8.3 (pp.191-192) - Angle Between Two Lines
lessons.notes_html:
The acute angle between two lines comes from their slopes: tan theta = | (m2 - m1) / (1 + m1 m2) |. Get each slope from its equation first (m = -a/b). If the denominator 1 + m1 m2 is zero, the lines are perpendicular and theta = 90 degrees. For a triangle, apply the formula to the three pairs of side slopes and fix any obtuse angle by taking its supplement, so the three interior angles add to 180 degrees.

Formula: tan theta = | (m2 - m1) / (1 + m1 m2) |

In this exercise: 1. Find the acute angle between the lines 7x - 3y = 0 and 3x - 11y + 5 = 0.. 2. Find the acute angle between the lines 8x - 3y - 1 = 0 and 11x - 5y + 15 = 0.. 3. Show that the angle measured from the line l1: a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 to the line l2: a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 is tan^-1((a1b2 - a2b1)/(a1a2 + b1b2)). Also deduce the conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity.. 4. Find interior angles of the triangle whose vertices are A(-4, 5), B(0, 7) and C(5, -5).. 5. Find the angles of the triangle with slopes of its sides are -7/3, 5/2 and 4/3.. 6. What is the equation of the line that passes through (2, -2) and the point of intersection of 2x + 3y - 5 = 0 and 7x - 5y - 2 = 0?. 7. Find the equation of a line through (1, 3) and the point of intersection of lines 2x - 3y - 5 = 0 and 4x + 5y - 7 = 0.. 8. Find the equation of line which passes through the point of intersection of the lines 7x - 3y - 19 = 0 and 3x + 2y + 5 = 0 and that line is parallel to the line y = 2x + 7..

Worked Example: 1. Find the acute angle between the lines 7x - 3y = 0 and 3x - 11y + 5 = 0.

Formula used: Slopes first (m = -a/b), then tan theta = | (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) |; denominator zero means perpendicular.

Step 1: slopes m1 = 7/3 and m2 = 3/11.

Step 2: tan theta = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1m2)| = |(3/11 - 7/3)/(1 + 21/33)| = 34/27.

Step 3: theta = tan^-1(34/27).

Answer: theta = 51.5 degrees (approx).

Worked Example: 3. Show that the angle measured from the line l1: a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 to the line l2: a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 is tan^-1((a1b2 - a2b1)/(a1a2 + b1b2)). Also deduce the conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity.

Formula used: Slopes first (m = -a/b), then tan theta = | (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) |; denominator zero means perpendicular.

Step 1: slopes m1 = -a1/b1 and m2 = -a2/b2.

Step 2: (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1m2) = (-a2/b2 + a1/b1)/(1 + a1a2/(b1b2)) = (a1b2 - a2b1)/(a1a2 + b1b2).

Step 3: angle = tan^-1((a1b2 - a2b1)/(a1a2 + b1b2)).

Step 4: parallel when the angle is 0, i.e. a1b2 - a2b1 = 0; perpendicular when the denominator is 0, i.e. a1a2 + b1b2 = 0. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 4. Find interior angles of the triangle whose vertices are A(-4, 5), B(0, 7) and C(5, -5).

Formula used: Slopes first (m = -a/b), then tan theta = | (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) |; denominator zero means perpendicular.

Step 1: slopes AB = 1/2, BC = -12/5, CA = -10/9.

Step 2: tan A = |(CA slope - AB slope)/(1 + product)| = 29/8, so A = 74.6 degrees (approx).

Step 3: tan B = 29/2, so B = 86.1 degrees (approx).

Step 4: C = 180 - 74.6 - 86.1 = 19.4 degrees (approx).

Answer: angles are 74.6, 86.1 and 19.4 degrees (approx).

Worked Example: 7. Find the equation of a line through (1, 3) and the point of intersection of lines 2x - 3y - 5 = 0 and 4x + 5y - 7 = 0.

Formula used: Slopes first (m = -a/b), then tan theta = | (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2) |; denominator zero means perpendicular.

Step 1: solving the two lines: 11y + 3 = 0 gives y = -3/11 and x = 23/11.

Step 2: line through (1, 3) and (23/11, -3/11) has slope (-3/11 - 3)/(23/11 - 1) = -3.

Step 3: y - 3 = -3(x - 1).

Answer: 3x + y - 6 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the acute angle between the lines 7x - 3y = 0 and 3x - 11y + 5 = 0.
mcqs.why: Slopes are m1 = 7/3 and m2 = 3/11; tan theta = |(3/11 - 7/3)/(1 + 21/33)| = 34/27, so theta = tan^-1(34/27) = 51.5 degrees approx.

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line 7x - 3y = 0?
mcqs.why: For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is m = -a/b = -7/(-3) = 7/3 for the line 7x - 3y = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line 3x - 11y + 5 = 0?
mcqs.why: For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is m = -a/b = -3/(-11) = 3/11 for the line 3x - 11y + 5 = 0.

mcqs.q: In tan theta = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2)|, if 1 + m1 m2 = 0, what is theta?
mcqs.why: A zero denominator 1 + m1 m2 = 0 means m1 m2 = -1, so the lines are perpendicular and theta = 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: Using coefficients, the condition for two lines to be parallel is:
mcqs.why: The angle from l1 to l2 is tan^-1((a1b2 - a2b1)/(a1a2 + b1b2)); the angle is zero for parallel lines, so a1b2 - a2b1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Using coefficients, the condition for two lines to be perpendicular is:
mcqs.why: The angle formula has denominator a1a2 + b1b2; when it is zero the angle is 90 degrees, so the lines are perpendicular.

mcqs.q: For the triangle A(-4, 5), B(0, 7), C(5, -5), what is the interior angle at A?
mcqs.why: Side slopes are AB = 1/2, BC = -12/5, CA = -10/9; at A, tan A = 29/8, so A = tan^-1(29/8) = 74.6 degrees approx.

mcqs.q: For the triangle A(-4, 5), B(0, 7), C(5, -5), what is the interior angle at B?
mcqs.why: Using the side slopes AB = 1/2 and BC = -12/5 at B gives tan B = 29/2, so B = tan^-1(29/2) = 86.1 degrees approx.

mcqs.q: What is the point of intersection of 2x - 3y - 5 = 0 and 4x + 5y - 7 = 0?
mcqs.why: Solving simultaneously: elimination gives 11y + 3 = 0, so y = -3/11, and substituting back gives x = 23/11.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line through (1, 3) and the point of intersection of 2x - 3y - 5 = 0 and 4x + 5y - 7 = 0.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 8 (p.192)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 8: the forms of a straight line, the angle between two lines, and the parallel (m1 = m2) and perpendicular (m1 x m2 = -1) tests.

In this exercise: 1. Choose the correct options. 2. Find the equation of line passing through (3, 5) and (2, 4).. 3. Find the angles of a triangle if slopes of sides are 3, -1/3 and 2 respectively.. 4. Find the angle between the lines l1: 3x - 5y + 4 = 0 and l2: 5x + 3y - 7 = 0..

Worked Example: Q1. (ii) If m = 3, c = -5 then y =

a) 2x - 5   b) 3x - 5   c) -3x + 5   d) -3x - 5

Answer: b) 3x - 5

Worked Example: Q1. (iii) If m1 = 2 and m2 = -1/2 are slopes of two straight lines then angle between them is:

a) 30 degrees   b) 60 degrees   c) 90 degrees   d) 120 degrees

Answer: c) 90 degrees

Worked Example: 2. Find the equation of line passing through (3, 5) and (2, 4).

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 8 Overview and Lessons 1 to 3 of this unit.

Step 1: slope = (4 - 5)/(2 - 3) = 1.

Step 2: y - 5 = 1(x - 3).

Answer: x - y + 2 = 0.

Worked Example: 3. Find the angles of a triangle if slopes of sides are 3, -1/3 and 2 respectively.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 8 Overview and Lessons 1 to 3 of this unit.

Step 1: the pair (3, -1/3) has product -1, so the angle is 90 degrees.

Step 2: the pair (3, 2) gives tan = 1/7, angle = 8.1 degrees (approx).

Step 3: the pair (2, -1/3) gives tan = 7, angle = 81.9 degrees (approx).

Answer: angles are 90, 8.1 and 81.9 degrees (approx).

Worked Example: 4. Find the angle between the lines l1: 3x - 5y + 4 = 0 and l2: 5x + 3y - 7 = 0.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 8 Overview and Lessons 1 to 3 of this unit.

Step 1: slopes m1 = 3/5 and m2 = -5/3.

Step 2: m1 x m2 = -1.

Answer: the lines are perpendicular, so the angle between them is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: If m = 3 and c = -5, what is the equation of the line?
mcqs.why: Use the slope-intercept form y = mx + c with m = 3 and c = -5, giving y = 3x - 5.

mcqs.q: If m1 = 2 and m2 = -1/2 are the slopes of two lines, what is the angle between them?
mcqs.why: The product m1 x m2 = 2 x (-1/2) = -1, so the lines are perpendicular and the angle between them is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the line passing through (3, 5) and (2, 4).
A triangle has side slopes 3, -1/3 and 2. The angle between the sides of slopes 3 and -1/3 is:
mcqs.why: The product 3 x (-1/3) = -1, so those two sides are perpendicular and the angle between them is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: A triangle has side slopes 3, -1/3 and 2. The angle between the sides of slopes 3 and 2 is:
mcqs.why: tan theta = |(2 - 3)/(1 + 3 x 2)| = 1/7, so theta = tan^-1(1/7) = 8.1 degrees approx.

mcqs.q: A triangle has side slopes 3, -1/3 and 2. The angle between the sides of slopes 2 and -1/3 is:
What is the angle between l1: 3x - 5y + 4 = 0 and l2: 5x + 3y - 7 = 0?
mcqs.why: Slopes are m1 = 3/5 and m2 = -5/3; their product is (3/5) x (-5/3) = -1, so the lines are perpendicular and the angle is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line 3x - 5y + 4 = 0?
mcqs.why: For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is m = -a/b = -3/(-5) = 3/5 for the line 3x - 5y + 4 = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line 5x + 3y - 7 = 0?
mcqs.why: For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is m = -a/b = -5/3 for the line 5x + 3y - 7 = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the slope of the line through (3, 5) and (2, 4)?
mcqs.why: Slope m = (4 - 5)/(2 - 3) = (-1)/(-1) = 1, which is the first step in finding the equation of this line.

lessons.title: Unit 9 Overview — Logic, Similarity, Polygons and Locus
lessons.notes_html:
Logic. A mathematical statement is a sentence that is either true or false. An axiom is a statement accepted as true without proof, used as a starting point. A conjecture is a statement believed true but not yet proved. A theorem is a statement that has been proved from axioms and known facts.

Similar figures. When two figures are similar with linear ratio k (the ratio of corresponding lengths), areas are in the ratio k^2 and volumes (for similar solids) in the ratio k^3.

Formula: Area ratio = (linear ratio)^2 ; Volume ratio = (linear ratio)^3.

Key Points

  • Triangle angles: the three interior angles add to 180 degrees; an exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
  • Quadrilaterals: the four interior angles add to 360 degrees. In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary (add to 180). The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Between parallel sides, co-interior angles are supplementary.
  • Polygons: sum of interior angles = (n - 2) x 180 degrees; each interior angle of a regular polygon = (n - 2) x 180 / n; the exterior angles always add to 360 degrees, so each exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360 / n, and n = 360 / (each exterior angle).
  • Formula: Area of a regular polygon = (1/2) x perimeter x apothem, where the apothem is the perpendicular from the centre to a side.
  • Locus = the path of a moving point obeying a rule. Fixed distance from a point: a circle. Equidistant from two points: the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. Equidistant from two intersecting lines: the angle bisector. Fixed distance from a line: a pair of lines parallel to it. Points X with angle AXB = 90 degrees lie on the circle with diameter AB.
  • A required point is usually found as the intersection of two loci: draw both loci and take their crossing point.

mcqs.q: What is a mathematical statement?
options: A statement accepted as true without proof
A sentence that is either true or false
A statement believed true but not yet proved
A statement that has been proved from axioms
mcqs.why: A mathematical statement is defined in the notes as a sentence that is either true or false.

mcqs.q: What is an axiom?
options: A sentence that is either true or false only
A statement believed true but not yet proved
A statement proved from other theorems only
A statement accepted as true without proof, used as a starting point
mcqs.why: An axiom is accepted as true without proof and is used as a starting point for reasoning.

mcqs.q: What is a conjecture?
options: A statement believed true but not yet proved
A statement accepted as true without proof
A statement that has been proved completely
A sentence that is neither true nor false
mcqs.why: A conjecture is believed to be true, but it has not yet been proved, unlike a theorem.

mcqs.q: What is a theorem?
options: A statement accepted as true without proof
A statement believed true but not yet proved
A statement that has been proved from axioms and known facts
A path traced by a moving point
mcqs.why: A theorem is a statement that has been proved from axioms and known facts.

mcqs.q: Two similar figures have linear ratio 3 : 1 (larger to smaller). What is the ratio of their areas, larger to smaller?
mcqs.why: Area ratio = (linear ratio)^2 = 3^2 : 1^2 = 9 : 1, so areas use the square of the linear ratio.

mcqs.q: Two similar solids have linear ratio 2 : 1 (larger to smaller). What is the ratio of their volumes, larger to smaller?
mcqs.why: Volume ratio = (linear ratio)^3 = 2^3 : 1^3 = 8 : 1, so volumes use the cube of the linear ratio.

mcqs.q: In a triangle, the two opposite interior angles are 40 degrees and 55 degrees. What is the exterior angle at the third vertex?
mcqs.why: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles = 40 + 55 = 95 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
mcqs.why: Each interior angle = (n - 2) x 180 / n = (6 - 2) x 180 / 6 = 720 / 6 = 120 degrees.

mcqs.q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 36 degrees. How many sides does it have?
mcqs.why: For a regular polygon n = 360 / (each exterior angle) = 360 / 36 = 10 sides.

mcqs.q: A regular polygon has perimeter 48 cm and apothem 6 cm. What is its area?
mcqs.why: Area = (1/2) x perimeter x apothem = (1/2) x 48 x 6 = 144 cm^2.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.1 (p.197) - Statements, Axioms, Conjectures and Theorems
lessons.notes_html:
Sort each sentence by the definitions in the Overview: is it simply true-or-false (a mathematical statement), accepted without proof as a starting rule (an axiom), or proved from known facts (a theorem)? A conjecture is the remaining case — believed, but not yet proved. Q2 practises the other half of logic: proving an identity by working the left side into the right side (common denominators for sums of fractions; factorize and cancel for products).

In this exercise: 1. Identify the following as mathematical statement, axiom, conjecture and theorem. 2. Prove the following.

Worked Example: 1. Identify the following as mathematical statement, axiom, conjecture and theorem: (i) -5 < 7.

Formula used: Classify by the definitions; prove identities by a common denominator or by factorizing and cancelling.

Answer: mathematical statement (it is a sentence that is either true or false; here it is true).

Worked Example: 1. (ii) Sum of two prime numbers greater than 4 is even.

Formula used: Classify by the definitions; prove identities by a common denominator or by factorizing and cancelling.

Step 1: Answer: theorem.

Step 2: every prime greater than 2 is odd.

Step 3: the sum of two odd numbers is even.

Step 4: hence the sum of any two primes greater than 4 is even — a proved statement.

Worked Example: 1. (iii) A line can extend to infinity.

Formula used: Classify by the definitions; prove identities by a common denominator or by factorizing and cancelling.

Answer: axiom (it is taken to be true as a starting point for reasoning, like Euclid's postulate).

Worked Example: 2. Prove the following: (i) (m - 1)/5 + (m + 3)/3 = 4(2m + 3)/15.

Formula used: Classify by the definitions; prove identities by a common denominator or by factorizing and cancelling.

Step 1: L.H.S = (3(m - 1) + 5(m + 3))/15.

Step 2: = (3m - 3 + 5m + 15)/15 = (8m + 12)/15.

Step 3: = 4(2m + 3)/15 = R.H.S. Hence proved.

Worked Example: 2. (ii) ((9x^2 - 1)/(3x^2 + 7x + 2)) x ((3x^2 - 4x + 1)/(3x - 1)^2) = (x - 1)/(x + 2).

Formula used: Classify by the definitions; prove identities by a common denominator or by factorizing and cancelling.

Step 1: factorise: 9x^2 - 1 = (3x - 1)(3x + 1); 3x^2 + 7x + 2 = (3x + 1)(x + 2); 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x - 1)(x - 1).

Step 2: the product = (3x - 1)(3x + 1)/((3x + 1)(x + 2)) x (3x - 1)(x - 1)/(3x - 1)^2.

Step 3: cancelling (3x + 1) and (3x - 1)^2 gives (x - 1)/(x + 2) = R.H.S. Hence proved.

mcqs.q: How is the sentence '-5 < 7' classified?
mcqs.why: It is a sentence that is either true or false, and here it is true, so it is a mathematical statement.

mcqs.q: How is 'The sum of two prime numbers greater than 4 is even' classified in the notes?
mcqs.why: Every prime greater than 2 is odd, and odd + odd = even, so the statement is proved and is a theorem.

mcqs.q: How is 'A line can extend to infinity' classified?
mcqs.why: It is taken to be true as a starting point for reasoning, like Euclid's postulate, so it is an axiom.

mcqs.q: When (m - 1)/5 + (m + 3)/3 is written with common denominator 15, what is the simplified numerator form of the whole expression?
Factorise 9x^2 - 1.
mcqs.why: Using the difference of two squares, 9x^2 - 1 = (3x)^2 - 1^2 = (3x - 1)(3x + 1).

mcqs.q: Factorise 3x^2 + 7x + 2.
mcqs.why: Expanding (3x + 1)(x + 2) gives 3x^2 + 6x + x + 2 = 3x^2 + 7x + 2, so this is the factorisation.

mcqs.q: Factorise 3x^2 - 4x + 1.
mcqs.why: Expanding (3x - 1)(x - 1) gives 3x^2 - 3x - x + 1 = 3x^2 - 4x + 1, so this is the factorisation.

mcqs.q: After factorising and cancelling, ((9x^2 - 1)/(3x^2 + 7x + 2)) x ((3x^2 - 4x + 1)/(3x - 1)^2) simplifies to what?
mcqs.why: The factors (3x + 1) and (3x - 1)^2 cancel from numerator and denominator, leaving (x - 1)/(x + 2).

mcqs.q: Which description fits a conjecture?
options: Accepted true without proof as a starting point
Proved from axioms and known facts
Believed true but not yet proved
Either true or false as a sentence only
mcqs.why: A conjecture is the remaining case in the notes: it is believed true but has not yet been proved.

mcqs.q: Using (m - 1)/5 + (m + 3)/3 = (8m + 12)/15, what is the value of the expression when m = 3?
mcqs.why: Substitute m = 3: (8 x 3 + 12)/15 = (24 + 12)/15 = 36/15 = 12/5 after cancelling 3.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.2 (pp.202-204) - Areas of Similar Figures
lessons.notes_html:
For similar figures, areas are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding lengths. Write the linear ratio from the given pair of corresponding sides (or widths, or perimeters), square it, and multiply or divide the known area. To find an unknown length from two areas, take the square root of the area ratio first. Triangles on the same altitude have areas in the ratio of their bases (Q6).

Formula: A2 / A1 = (l2 / l1)^2

In this exercise: 1. Find the unknown area of each of the following pairs of similar figures. 2. Find the ratio of the areas of two circles whose radii are 4 cm and 7 cm.. 3. A triangular plot of land PQR is such that PT = 6 m and PR = 10 m. ST and QR are two water pipes that are parallel to each other. The area of triangle PST is 24 m^2. Find the area of the land occupied by. 4. Find the unknown value in each of the following pairs of similar figures. 5. The perimeters of two similar regular hexagons are 10 m and 8 m. Given that the area of the larger hexagon is 200 m^2, find the area of the smaller hexagon.. 6. In the figure, triangle XYZ is an enlargement of triangle XMN.
