Given that XM = 6 cm and that the areas of triangles XMN and MYN are 14 cm^2 and 22 cm^2 respectively, find the length of MY..

Worked Example: 1. Find the unknown area of each of the following pairs of similar figures: (i) two triangles with corresponding sides 8 cm and 2 cm, and area of the larger 64 cm^2.

Formula used: Square the ratio of corresponding lengths to get the ratio of areas; square-root the area ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: A2/A1 = (2/8)^2 = 1/16.

Step 2: A2 = 64/16.

Answer: A2 = 4 cm^2.

Worked Example: 2. Find the ratio of the areas of two circles whose radii are 4 cm and 7 cm.

Formula used: Square the ratio of corresponding lengths to get the ratio of areas; square-root the area ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: areas are proportional to the squares of the radii.

Step 2: ratio = 4^2 : 7^2.

Answer: 16 : 49.

Worked Example: 3. A triangular plot of land PQR is such that PT = 6 m and PR = 10 m. ST and QR are two water pipes that are parallel to each other. The area of triangle PST is 24 m^2. Find the area of the land occupied by (i) triangle PQR, (ii) SQRT.

Formula used: Square the ratio of corresponding lengths to get the ratio of areas; square-root the area ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: triangles PST and PQR are similar with linear ratio 10/6 = 5/3.

Step 2: (i) area of triangle PQR = 24 x (5/3)^2 = 24 x 25/9 = 200/3.

Step 3: (ii) area of SQRT = 200/3 - 24 = 128/3.

Answer: (i) 200/3 m^2 (66.67 approx); (ii) 128/3 m^2 (42.67 approx).

Worked Example: 5. The perimeters of two similar regular hexagons are 10 m and 8 m. Given that the area of the larger hexagon is 200 m^2, find the area of the smaller hexagon.

Formula used: Square the ratio of corresponding lengths to get the ratio of areas; square-root the area ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: area ratio = (8/10)^2 = 16/25.

Step 2: smaller area = 200 x 16/25.

Answer: 128 m^2.

mcqs.q: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 8 cm and 2 cm. The area of the larger is 64 cm^2. What is the area of the smaller?
What is the ratio of the areas of two circles whose radii are 4 cm and 7 cm?
mcqs.why: Areas are proportional to the squares of the radii, so the ratio = 4^2 : 7^2 = 16 : 49.

mcqs.q: In triangle PQR, PT = 6 m, PR = 10 m, ST is parallel to QR, and the area of triangle PST is 24 m^2. What is the area of triangle PQR?
Using the same plot as the previous data (area PQR = 200/3 m^2 and area PST = 24 m^2), what is the area of quadrilateral SQRT?
mcqs.why: Area of SQRT = area of PQR - area of PST = 200/3 - 24 = 200/3 - 72/3 = 128/3 m^2.

mcqs.q: The perimeters of two similar regular hexagons are 10 m and 8 m. The area of the larger is 200 m^2. What is the area of the smaller?
mcqs.why: Area ratio = (8/10)^2 = 16/25, so the smaller area = 200 x 16/25 = 3200/25 = 128 m^2.

mcqs.q: Two similar figures have corresponding sides 3 cm and 6 cm. The area of the smaller is 20 cm^2. What is the area of the larger?
mcqs.why: Area ratio = (6/3)^2 = 2^2 = 4, so the larger area = 20 x 4 = 80 cm^2.

mcqs.q: The areas of two similar figures are 36 cm^2 and 9 cm^2. What is the ratio of their corresponding lengths, larger to smaller?
mcqs.why: Length ratio = square root of the area ratio = sqrt(36/9) = sqrt(4) = 2, so the ratio is 2 : 1.

mcqs.q: Two triangles on the same altitude have bases 5 cm and 15 cm. What is the ratio of their areas, smaller to larger?
mcqs.why: Triangles on the same altitude have areas in the ratio of their bases, so the area ratio = 5 : 15 = 1 : 3.

mcqs.q: Two similar triangles have perimeters in the ratio 5 : 4. What is the ratio of their areas?
mcqs.why: Perimeter ratio is a linear ratio, so area ratio = 5^2 : 4^2 = 25 : 16.

mcqs.q: Two similar figures have areas in the ratio 49 : 25. A side of the smaller figure is 10 cm. What is the corresponding side of the larger figure?
mcqs.why: Length ratio = sqrt(49/25) = 7/5, so the larger side = 10 x 7/5 = 70/5 = 14 cm.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.3 (pp.206-207) - Volumes of Similar Solids
lessons.notes_html:
For similar solids, volumes are in the ratio of the cubes of corresponding lengths — and mass is in the same ratio when the material is the same. Surface areas still follow the square rule. To find an unknown length from two volumes, take the cube root of the volume ratio. Base areas give the square of the linear ratio, so heights come from a square root (Q5).

Formula: V2 / V1 = (l2 / l1)^3 ; surface-area ratio = (l2 / l1)^2

In this exercise: 1. Find the unknown volume of each of the following pairs of similar solids. 2. Find the ratio of the volume of. 3. In a juice shop, a small bottle has a height of 6 cm while a large bottle has a height of 9 cm. If the capacity of the large bottle is 540 cm^3, find the capacity of the small bottle.. 4. Find the unknown values in each of the following pairs of similar solids. 5. The areas of the bases of two similar cones are in the ratio 9 : 16.. 6. Two solid spheres made of the same material have masses of 640 kg and 270 kg respectively. Determine the ratio of their diameters.. 7. A bakery sells similar boxes of cookies in two sizes, small and large. The small box has a mass of 280 g and height of 15 cm. If the large box has a mass of 750 g, find its height.. 8. Two similar solid candy canes have heights 4 cm and 7 cm.. 9. The volume of one sphere is 4 times that of another sphere. Given that the radius of the smaller sphere is 3 cm, find the radius of the larger sphere.. 10. The mass of a glass figurine of height 6 cm is 500 g. Find the mass of a similar glass figurine if it has a height of 4 cm..

Worked Example: 1. Find the unknown volume of each of the following pairs of similar solids: (i) two cubes of sides 12 cm and 6 cm, volume of the smaller 72 cm^3.

Formula used: Cube the length ratio for volumes (and masses); cube-root the volume ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: V1/V2 = (12/6)^3 = 8.

Step 2: V1 = 72 x 8.

Answer: V1 = 576 cm^3.

Worked Example: 2. Find the ratio of the volume of: (i) two similar solid cylinders of circumferences 10 cm and 8 cm; (ii) two similar solid cones of heights 9 cm and 12 cm.

Formula used: Cube the length ratio for volumes (and masses); cube-root the volume ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: (i) volume ratio = (10/8)^3 = 1000/512 = 125/64.

Step 2: (ii) volume ratio = (9/12)^3 = 729/1728 = 27/64.

Answer: (i) 125 : 64; (ii) 27 : 64.

Worked Example: 4. (ii) two cones of volumes 16 cm^3 and 54 cm^3, with slant heights 6 cm and b cm.

Formula used: Cube the length ratio for volumes (and masses); cube-root the volume ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: (b/6)^3 = 54/16 = 27/8.

Step 2: b/6 = 3/2.

Answer: b = 9 cm.

Worked Example: 5. The areas of the bases of two similar cones are in the ratio 9 : 16. (i) Find the ratio of the heights of the cones. (ii) Given that the volume of the larger cone is 448 cm^3, find the volume of the smaller cone.

Formula used: Cube the length ratio for volumes (and masses); cube-root the volume ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: (i) base-area ratio is the square of the linear ratio, so the linear (height) ratio = 3 : 4.

Step 2: (ii) volume ratio = 27 : 64, so smaller volume = 448 x 27/64 = 189.

Answer: (i) 3 : 4; (ii) 189 cm^3.

Worked Example: 8. Two similar solid candy canes have heights 4 cm and 7 cm. (i) Find the ratio of the total surface areas of the candy canes. (ii) Given that the smaller candy cane has a mass of 10 g, find the mass of the larger candy cane.

Formula used: Cube the length ratio for volumes (and masses); cube-root the volume ratio to get back a length.

Step 1: (i) surface-area ratio = (4/7)^2 = 16 : 49.

Step 2: (ii) mass ratio = (4/7)^3 = 64 : 343, so larger mass = 10 x 343/64 = 53.59.

Answer: (i) 16 : 49; (ii) 53.6 g (approx).

mcqs.q: Two similar cubes have sides 12 cm and 6 cm. The volume of the smaller is 72 cm^3. What is the volume of the larger?
mcqs.why: V larger / V smaller = (12/6)^3 = 2^3 = 8, so the larger volume = 72 x 8 = 576 cm^3.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of the volumes of two similar solid cylinders whose circumferences are 10 cm and 8 cm?
mcqs.why: Circumference is a length, so volume ratio = (10/8)^3 = (5/4)^3 = 125/64, written as 125 : 64.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of the volumes of two similar solid cones whose heights are 9 cm and 12 cm?
mcqs.why: Volume ratio = (9/12)^3 = (3/4)^3 = 27/64, written as 27 : 64.

mcqs.q: A small juice bottle has height 6 cm and a similar large bottle has height 9 cm. The large bottle holds 540 cm^3. What does the small bottle hold?
Two similar cones have volumes 16 cm^3 and 54 cm^3. The slant height of the smaller is 6 cm. What is the slant height of the larger?
The areas of the bases of two similar cones are in the ratio 9 : 16. What is the ratio of their heights?
mcqs.why: Base-area ratio is the square of the linear ratio, so height ratio = sqrt(9) : sqrt(16) = 3 : 4.

mcqs.q: For the same two similar cones (base areas 9 : 16), the volume of the larger cone is 448 cm^3. What is the volume of the smaller cone?
mcqs.why: Volume ratio = 3^3 : 4^3 = 27 : 64, so smaller volume = 448 x 27/64 = 7 x 27 = 189 cm^3.

mcqs.q: Two similar solid candy canes have heights 4 cm and 7 cm. What is the ratio of their total surface areas?
mcqs.why: Surface areas follow the square rule, so the ratio = 4^2 : 7^2 = 16 : 49.

mcqs.q: The smaller candy cane (height 4 cm) has mass 10 g. The larger has height 7 cm and is made of the same material. What is its mass, approximately?
mcqs.why: Mass ratio = volume ratio = (7/4)^3 = 343/64, so larger mass = 10 x 343/64 = 3430/64 = 53.6 g approx.

mcqs.q: A glass figurine of height 6 cm has mass 500 g. What is the mass of a similar figurine of height 4 cm, made of the same glass?

lessons.title: Exercise 9.4 (pp.218-220) - Angles of Triangles, Quadrilaterals and Polygons
lessons.notes_html:
The working facts: triangle angles add to 180 degrees; an exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles; angles on a straight line add to 180; vertically opposite angles are equal; quadrilateral angles add to 360 degrees; a polygon of n sides has interior-angle sum (n - 2) x 180 degrees; parallelogram opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles supplementary; the diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles.

Set up one equation in the unknown from the right fact and solve it. (Q11: the book prints "AB parallel to BE", a misprint — the parallel marks are on AB and DC, and the solution uses that.)

Formula: Interior sum = (n - 2) x 180 degrees ; each exterior (regular) = 360 / n ; Area = (1/2) x perimeter x apothem

In this exercise: 1. Find the value of the unknown in each of the following figures. 2. Given that DAB is a straight line, find the values of the unknown in each of the following figures. 3. If the sizes of the angles of a triangle are 3x degrees, 4x degrees and 5x degrees, find the smallest angle of the triangle.. 4. In the figure, ABC is a straight line. Given that angle ADB = angle BDC, find. 5. Given that ABC and BED are straight lines, find the value(s) of the unknown(s) in each of the following figures. 6. If the sizes of the angles of a triangle are (x - 35) degrees, (x - 25) degrees and (x/2 - 10) degrees, find the value of x.. 7. In triangle ABC, angle BAC = 50 degrees and angle BCA = 60 degrees.. 8. In the figure, ACE and BCD are straight lines. Angle at A is 50 degrees, and the top triangle has angles 61 degrees and 41 degrees. Find. 9. Find the values of the unknowns in each of the following parallelograms. 10. The figure shows a rhombus ABCD where the diagonals AC and BD intersect at E. Angle CDB is (3x + 7) degrees and angle BAC is (2x + 53) degrees. Find the value of x.. 11. The figure shows a trapezium ABCD where AB is parallel to CD (the book prints 'AB parallel to BE', a misprint — the parallel arrow marks are on AB and DC). Angle at D is 5x degrees, at C is y degrees, at A is x degrees, at B is 2.2x degrees. Find the value of x and of y.. 12. Find the value of the unknown in each of the following figures. 13. Find the number of sides of a regular polygon if each exterior angle of the polygon is. 14. Basement of a godown is in the shape of a regular octagon having side length 10 m and apothem 8 m. Find the perimeter and area of the godown.. 15. A garden is in the shape of an equilateral triangle with side length 12 m. Find its perimeter and also find the cost of fencing at Rs.300 per metre..

Worked Example: 1. Find the value of the unknown in each of the following figures: (i) a right-angled triangle with right angle at B, angle at A 39 degrees, angle at C a degrees.

Formula used: Choose the angle fact (180 in a triangle, 360 in a quadrilateral, (n - 2) x 180 in a polygon), write the equation, solve.

Step 1: a + 90 + 39 = 180.

Answer: a = 51.

Worked Example: 2. Given that DAB is a straight line, find the values of the unknown in each of the following figures: (i) a triangle with angle at C 55 degrees, angle at B 47 degrees, exterior angle at A a degrees.

Formula used: Choose the angle fact (180 in a triangle, 360 in a quadrilateral, (n - 2) x 180 in a polygon), write the equation, solve.

Step 1: exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles.

Step 2: a = 55 + 47.

Answer: a = 102.

Worked Example: 3. If the sizes of the angles of a triangle are 3x degrees, 4x degrees and 5x degrees, find the smallest angle of the triangle.

Formula used: Choose the angle fact (180 in a triangle, 360 in a quadrilateral, (n - 2) x 180 in a polygon), write the equation, solve.

Step 1: 3x + 4x + 5x = 180, so 12x = 180 and x = 15.

Step 2: smallest angle = 3x = 45.

Answer: 45 degrees.

Worked Example: 9. Find the values of the unknowns in each of the following parallelograms: (i) angle at A 106 degrees, angle DBC 48 degrees, angle at C a degrees, angle CDB b degrees.

Formula used: Choose the angle fact (180 in a triangle, 360 in a quadrilateral, (n - 2) x 180 in a polygon), write the equation, solve.

Step 1: opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so a = 106.

Step 2: in triangle BCD, b = 180 - 106 - 48 = 26.

Answer: a = 106, b = 26.

Worked Example: 12. (ii) a hexagon with angles 108 degrees, 4d degrees, 4d degrees, 5d degrees, 102 degrees and 4d degrees.

Formula used: Choose the angle fact (180 in a triangle, 360 in a quadrilateral, (n - 2) x 180 in a polygon), write the equation, solve.

Step 1: sum of interior angles of a hexagon = (6 - 2) x 180 = 720 degrees.

Step 2: 108 + 4d + 4d + 5d + 102 + 4d = 720, so 17d = 510.

Answer: d = 30.

Worked Example: 13. Find the number of sides of a regular polygon if each exterior angle of the polygon is: (i) 90 degrees; (ii) 45 degrees.

Formula used: Choose the angle fact (180 in a triangle, 360 in a quadrilateral, (n - 2) x 180 in a polygon), write the equation, solve.

Step 1: n = 360/(exterior angle).

Step 2: (i) n = 360/90 = 4.

Step 3: (ii) n = 360/45 = 8.

Answer: (i) 4 sides; (ii) 8 sides.

mcqs.q: A right-angled triangle has the right angle at B and angle at A equal to 39 degrees. What is angle a at C?
mcqs.why: Angles in a triangle add to 180 degrees, so a + 90 + 39 = 180 and a = 180 - 129 = 51 degrees.

mcqs.q: DAB is a straight line. A triangle has angles at C and B of 55 degrees and 47 degrees, and a is the exterior angle at A. What is a?
mcqs.why: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so a = 55 + 47 = 102 degrees.

mcqs.q: The angles of a triangle are 3x degrees, 4x degrees and 5x degrees. What is the smallest angle?
mcqs.why: 3x + 4x + 5x = 180 gives 12x = 180, so x = 15, and the smallest angle = 3x = 3 x 15 = 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: The angles of a triangle are (x - 35) degrees, (x - 25) degrees and (x/2 - 10) degrees. What is the value of x?
In a parallelogram, angle at A is 106 degrees. What is angle a at C, opposite A?
mcqs.why: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so the angle at C equals the angle at A, a = 106 degrees.

mcqs.q: A hexagon has angles 108 degrees, 4d degrees, 4d degrees, 5d degrees, 102 degrees and 4d degrees. What is d?
A regular polygon has each exterior angle 90 degrees. How many sides does it have?
mcqs.why: Number of sides n = 360 / (each exterior angle) = 360 / 90 = 4 sides.

mcqs.q: A regular polygon has each exterior angle 45 degrees. How many sides does it have?
mcqs.why: Number of sides n = 360 / (each exterior angle) = 360 / 45 = 8 sides.

mcqs.q: The basement of a godown is a regular octagon with side length 10 m and apothem 8 m. What is its area?
mcqs.why: Perimeter = 8 x 10 = 80 m. Area = (1/2) x perimeter x apothem = (1/2) x 80 x 8 = 320 m^2.

mcqs.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to CD (the notes correct the book misprint 'AB parallel to BE'). Angle at A is x degrees and angle at D is 5x degrees. What is x?
mcqs.why: A and D are co-interior angles between the parallel sides AB and CD, so x + 5x = 180, 6x = 180 and x = 30.

lessons.title: Exercise 9.5 (pp.225-226) - Locus and Construction
lessons.notes_html:
Each condition names a locus (see the Overview list): a circle for a fixed distance from a point, the perpendicular bisector for points equidistant from two points, the angle bisector for points equidistant from two lines, and a pair of parallel lines for a fixed distance from a line. A point satisfying two conditions is the intersection of the two loci — draw both and mark the crossing. Scale drawings (Q3, Q4) are built to the stated scale and the answers are then measured, or checked by the sine rule.

Honest notes: Q2 as printed gives only the panel sides, so the SSS construction is given; Q5 as printed gives no spacing between lights, so no definite number of lights follows — the locus is the answer.

In this exercise: 1. Construct, on separate diagrams. 2. A wooden panel is in the shape of triangle ABC, where AB = 4.5 m, BC = 6.5 m and CA = 4 m. NOTE: as printed, Q2 states only the panel's shape and side lengths and gives no further instruction; the notes give the SSS construction.. 3. Two points P and Q are 50 m apart on the south bank of a river flowing due east between parallel banks. R is a point on the north bank such that the bearing of R from P is 042 degrees and the bearing of Q from R is 140 degrees.. 4. A playground is in the shape of a quadrilateral ABCD. It is given that AB = 90 m, AD = 70 m, angle BAD = 115 degrees, angle ABC = 100 degrees and angle ADC = 85 degrees.. 5. A street authority wants to install streetlights at a uniform distance of 3 meters from the edges of a straight road. Find the number of locations where streetlights should be placed, if the street is 30 m long. NOTE: as printed, no spacing between consecutive lights is given, so no definite number follows; the notes give the locus.. 6. A park has a walking track running in a straight line, and a fence needs to be installed 5 m away from the track on both sides. Where should the fence be placed?.

Worked Example: 1. Construct, on separate diagrams: (i) the locus of a point that moves so that it is constantly 4 cm from a fixed point A; (ii) the locus of points less than 4 cm from the fixed point A.

Formula used: Name the locus for each condition; the required point is where the two loci cross.

Step 1: (i) the locus is the circle of radius 4 cm with centre A.

Step 2: (ii) the locus is the interior of that circle (the disc), not including the circumference.

Answer: (i) circle radius 4 cm centred at A; (ii) the disc inside that circle.

Worked Example: 3. Two points P and Q are 50 m apart on the south bank of a river flowing due east between parallel banks. R is a point on the north bank such that the bearing of R from P is 042 degrees and the bearing of Q from R is 140 degrees. (i) Using a scale of 2 cm to 10 m, construct triangle PQR. Measure PR and find, correct to the nearest metre, the width of the river.

Formula used: Name the locus for each condition; the required point is where the two loci cross.

Step 1: angle at P between PQ (east) and PR (bearing 042 degrees) is 90 - 42 = 48 degrees.

Step 2: angle at R between RP (bearing 222 degrees) and RQ (bearing 140 degrees) is 82 degrees.

Step 3: angle at Q is 180 - 48 - 82 = 50 degrees.

Step 4: by the sine rule, PR = 50 x sin 50 degrees/sin 82 degrees = 38.68 m.

Step 5: width = PR x sin 48 degrees = 28.74 m.

Answer: PR = 39 m (approx); width of the river = 29 m (nearest metre).

Worked Example: 4. A playground is in the shape of a quadrilateral ABCD. It is given that AB = 90 m, AD = 70 m, angle BAD = 115 degrees, angle ABC = 100 degrees and angle ADC = 85 degrees. (i) Using a scale of 1 cm to represent 10 m, make an accurate scale drawing of the playground.

Formula used: Name the locus for each condition; the required point is where the two loci cross.

Step 1: draw AB = 9 cm.

Step 2: at A draw AD = 7 cm at 115 degrees to AB.

Step 3: at B draw BC at 100 degrees to BA, meeting the ray from D that makes 85 degrees at D, giving BC about 11.6 cm (116 m).

Step 4: join CD.

Answer: quadrilateral ABCD drawn to the scale 1 cm : 10 m.

Worked Example: 5. A street authority wants to install streetlights at a uniform distance of 3 meters from the edges of a straight road. Find the number of locations where streetlights should be placed, if the street is 30 m long. NOTE: as printed, no spacing between consecutive lights is given, so no definite number follows; the notes give the locus.

Formula used: Name the locus for each condition; the required point is where the two loci cross.

Step 1: the locus of points 3 m from a straight road is the pair of lines parallel to the road at 3 m on either side.

Step 2: along the 30 m street these are two 30 m lines, one on each side. Answer: the streetlights lie on the two lines 3 m from the edges, running the 30 m length; the question as printed gives no spacing between lights, so the number of locations is not fixed by the data.

mcqs.q: What is the locus of a point that moves so that it is constantly 4 cm from a fixed point A?
options: The interior of a circle of radius 4 cm
A pair of lines parallel to A
The perpendicular bisector of a segment
The circle of radius 4 cm with centre A
mcqs.why: A fixed distance from a fixed point gives a circle, here the circle of radius 4 cm centred at A.

mcqs.q: What is the locus of points less than 4 cm from the fixed point A?
options: The interior of the circle of radius 4 cm centred at A, not including the circumference
The circumference of the circle of radius 4 cm
The circle of radius 4 cm with centre A only
Two parallel lines 4 cm from A
mcqs.why: Points less than 4 cm from A lie inside the circle, so the locus is the disc interior, excluding the circumference.

mcqs.q: A wooden panel is triangle ABC with AB = 4.5 m, BC = 6.5 m and CA = 4 m. As printed, Q2 gives only these sides. What construction do the notes give for the panel?
options: A locus of points 4 cm from A
The SSS construction using the three given sides
A scale drawing using two bearings
mcqs.why: As printed Q2 states only the panel shape and side lengths, so the notes give the SSS construction from AB, BC and CA.

mcqs.q: How is a point that must satisfy two locus conditions usually found?
options: On the circumference of any circle
At the midpoint of the two points
As the intersection of the two loci
On a line parallel to the given line
mcqs.why: The notes state that a required point is usually found as the intersection of two loci: draw both and take the crossing point.

mcqs.q: Streetlights are to be at a uniform distance of 3 m from the edges of a straight road. What is the locus of their positions?
options: A pair of lines parallel to the road, 3 m away on either side
The perpendicular bisector of the road
A single line along the centre of the road
mcqs.why: A fixed distance from a line gives a pair of lines parallel to it, here two lines 3 m from the road, one on each side.

mcqs.q: For that streetlight question, the street is 30 m long but no spacing between consecutive lights is given. What number of locations follows from the data as printed?
options: No definite number follows, because the spacing between lights is not given
mcqs.why: The notes are explicit: as printed no spacing is given, so no definite number follows; the locus, the two parallel lines, is the answer.

mcqs.q: A fence is to be installed 5 m away from a straight walking track, on both sides. Where should the fence be placed?
options: On a circle of radius 5 m around the track
On two lines parallel to the track, each 5 m from it, one on each side
On the perpendicular bisector of the track
On the track itself, marked every 5 m
mcqs.why: A fixed distance of 5 m from a straight line is a pair of parallel lines, one on each side of the track.

mcqs.q: P and Q are 50 m apart on the south bank. The bearing of R from P is 042 degrees, and PQ runs due east. What is the angle at P of triangle PQR?
mcqs.why: The angle at P between PQ (due east) and PR (bearing 042 degrees) is 90 - 42 = 48 degrees.

mcqs.q: Using the sine rule for triangle PQR (PQ = 50 m, angle at Q = 50 degrees, angle at R = 82 degrees), PR is approximately what?
mcqs.why: By the sine rule PR = 50 x sin 50 degrees / sin 82 degrees = 38.68 m, which is 39 m to the nearest metre.

mcqs.q: From PR = 38.68 m and the angle of 48 degrees at P, the width of the river is approximately what?
mcqs.why: Width = PR x sin 48 degrees = 38.68 x sin 48 degrees = 28.74 m, which is 29 m to the nearest metre.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 9 (pp.226-227)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 9: logic terms, area and volume ratios of similar figures and solids, polygon angle formulas, the apothem area formula, and the standard loci.

In this exercise: 1. Choose the correct options. 2. Find the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles if the lengths of their corresponding sides are. 3. Find the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles if their perimeters are 294 cm and 336 cm.. 4. The volumes of two similar cylinders are in the ratio 8 : 27. Find the ratio of the base radii of the cylinders.. 5. The volumes of two similar water jugs are in the ratio 27 : 64. Find. 6. A stop sign is designed in the shape of a regular octagon. What is the measure of each interior angle, and if each side of the octagon is 50 cm and its apothem is 40 cm, what is its area?. 7. A gardener wants to design a pentagon shaped flower garden where each side is 6 m. What is the measure of each interior angle, and find the area of the garden if its apothem is 4 m.. 8. Umair has a hexagonal plot having length of each side 50 m and apothem 42 m. He wants to fix pentagonal tiles with length of each side 12 cm and apothem 10 cm.. 9. A city Mayor wants to build a middle school that is equidistant from two existing schools, P and Q. How should the location be chosen?. 10. A drone is programmed to stay 50 m away from its charging station. What is the possible flight path of the drone?. 11. A security camera needs to be installed at a hallway intersection such that it is equidistant from both walls forming the intersection. Where should the camera be placed?.

Worked Example: Q1. (i) A statement which is either true or false is:

a) axiom   b) mathematical statement   c) theorem   d) conjecture

Answer: b) mathematical statement

Worked Example: Q1. (iii) Sum of angles in a triangle is 180 degrees is known as:

a) theorem   b) conjecture   c) axiom   d) none of these

Answer: a) theorem

Worked Example: Q1. (vii) The sum of exterior angles of a regular polygon is:

a) 90 degrees   b) 180 degrees   c) 270 degrees   d) 360 degrees

Answer: d) 360 degrees

Worked Example: 2. Find the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles if the lengths of their corresponding sides are: (i) 3 cm and 5 cm; (ii) 4.5 m and 9 m; (iii) 2 mm and 3 mm.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 9 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: area ratio is the square of the side ratio.

Step 2: (i) (3/5)^2 = 9 : 25.

Step 3: (ii) (4.5/9)^2 = 1 : 4.

Step 4: (iii) (2/3)^2 = 4 : 9.

Answer: (i) 9 : 25; (ii) 1 : 4; (iii) 4 : 9.

Worked Example: 5. The volumes of two similar cylinders are in the ratio 8 : 27. Find the ratio of the base radii of the cylinders.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 9 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: linear ratio = cube root of 8/27 = 2/3.

Answer: 2 : 3.

Worked Example: 7. A stop sign is designed in the shape of a regular octagon. What is the measure of each interior angle, and if each side of the octagon is 50 cm and its apothem is 40 cm, what is its area?

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 9 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: each interior angle = (8 - 2) x 180/8 = 135 degrees.

Step 2: perimeter = 8 x 50 = 400 cm.

Step 3: area = (1/2) x 400 x 40 = 8000.

Answer: interior angle = 135 degrees; area = 8000 cm^2.

Worked Example: 10. A city Mayor wants to build a middle school that is equidistant from two existing schools, P and Q. How should the location be chosen?

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 9 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: the locus of points equidistant from P and Q is the perpendicular bisector of PQ.

Answer: the school should be built anywhere on the perpendicular bisector of the segment PQ.

mcqs.q: A statement which is either true or false is called what?
mcqs.why: By definition, a statement which is either true or false is a mathematical statement.

mcqs.q: 'The sum of angles in a triangle is 180 degrees' is known as what?
mcqs.why: The result is proved from known facts, and the review exercise classifies it as a theorem.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of a regular polygon?
mcqs.why: The exterior angles of a polygon always add to 360 degrees, whatever the number of sides.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles whose corresponding sides are 3 cm and 5 cm?
mcqs.why: Area ratio is the square of the side ratio, so (3/5)^2 = 9/25, written as 9 : 25.

mcqs.q: Two similar triangles have perimeters 294 cm and 336 cm. What is the ratio of their areas?
mcqs.why: Perimeter ratio = 294 : 336 = 7 : 8, so area ratio = 7^2 : 8^2 = 49 : 64.

mcqs.q: The volumes of two similar cylinders are in the ratio 8 : 27. What is the ratio of their base radii?
mcqs.why: Radius is a length, so radius ratio = cube root of the volume ratio = cube root of 8/27 = 2/3, written 2 : 3.

mcqs.q: A stop sign is a regular octagon. What is the measure of each interior angle?
mcqs.why: Each interior angle = (8 - 2) x 180 / 8 = 6 x 180 / 8 = 1080 / 8 = 135 degrees.

mcqs.q: The same regular octagon has each side 50 cm and apothem 40 cm. What is its area?
mcqs.why: Perimeter = 8 x 50 = 400 cm. Area = (1/2) x perimeter x apothem = (1/2) x 400 x 40 = 8000 cm^2.

mcqs.q: A middle school is to be built equidistant from two existing schools P and Q. Where should it be located?
options: Anywhere on a circle with centre P
Anywhere on the perpendicular bisector of the segment PQ
Anywhere on the angle bisector of P and Q
At the midpoint of PQ only
mcqs.why: The locus of points equidistant from two points P and Q is the perpendicular bisector of PQ, so the school goes on that line.

mcqs.q: A security camera at a hallway intersection must be equidistant from both walls forming the intersection. Where should it be placed?
options: On the perpendicular bisector of the hallway
On a circle centred at the intersection
On a line parallel to one wall
On the angle bisector of the angle between the two walls
mcqs.why: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on the angle bisector, so the camera is placed on the bisector of the walls' angle.

lessons.title: Unit 10 Overview — Constructions and Concurrency
lessons.notes_html:
A triangle is completely fixed by three suitable pieces of data, and each choice gives a construction: SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and the included angle), ASA (one side and the two angles at its ends) or SSA (two sides and a non-included angle — the arc may meet the ray twice, once, or not at all, so check how many triangles the data really give).

Key Points

  • Median: the segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. The three medians are concurrent at the centroid G, which divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1.
  • Altitude: the perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side. The three altitudes are concurrent at the orthocentre O.
  • Angle bisector: the ray halving a vertex angle. The three bisectors are concurrent at the incentre I.
  • Perpendicular bisector: the perpendicular at the midpoint of a side. The three are concurrent at the circumcentre O — inside the triangle for an acute triangle, outside it when the triangle has an obtuse angle.
  • Construction routine: draw the base first; build each given angle with compass arcs (or a protractor where the book allows); cut off each given length with the compass on the ray or as an arc from the correct centre; join the meeting point. To show concurrency, draw two of the lines, mark their meeting point, then draw the third and check that it passes through the same point.
  • In an equilateral triangle the medians, altitudes, bisectors and perpendicular bisectors coincide, and the three altitudes are congruent.

mcqs.q: Which set of data is called SSS for constructing a triangle?
options: Two sides and the included angle
One side and the two angles at its ends
Two sides and a non-included angle
mcqs.why: SSS means Side-Side-Side: the triangle is fixed by giving the lengths of all three sides.

mcqs.q: A median of a triangle is a segment joining a vertex to which point?
options: Any point on the opposite side
The foot of the perpendicular on the opposite side
The midpoint of the opposite side
The centre of the triangle only
mcqs.why: By definition a median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, so it bisects that side.

mcqs.q: The three medians of a triangle meet at the centroid G. In what ratio does G divide each median?
mcqs.why: The centroid divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1, the longer part being towards the vertex.

mcqs.q: A median of a triangle is 12 cm long. How far is the centroid from the vertex along this median?
mcqs.why: The centroid takes 2/(2+1) = 2/3 of the median from the vertex, and 2/3 of 12 cm = 8 cm.

mcqs.q: The three altitudes of a triangle are concurrent at which point?
mcqs.why: Altitudes are the perpendiculars from the vertices to the opposite sides, and they meet at the orthocentre.

mcqs.q: The three angle bisectors of a triangle are concurrent at which point?
mcqs.why: Each angle bisector halves a vertex angle, and the three bisectors meet at the incentre I.

mcqs.q: For an obtuse-angled triangle, where does the circumcentre lie?
options: At a vertex of the triangle
mcqs.why: The circumcentre is inside for an acute triangle but falls outside when the triangle has an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: In the SSA case, why must you check the data carefully before stating the construction?
options: The base can never be drawn first
The arc may meet the ray twice, once, or not at all
The angles always add to 180 degrees
The compass cannot cut off the given length
mcqs.why: With two sides and a non-included angle, the cutting arc may meet the ray twice, once, or not at all, giving two, one or no triangles.

mcqs.q: In an equilateral triangle, what is true of its medians, altitudes, bisectors and perpendicular bisectors?
options: They are all parallel to each other
They meet at four different points
They coincide, and the three altitudes are congruent
mcqs.why: In an equilateral triangle the four sets of special lines coincide, and the three altitudes are congruent.

mcqs.q: A triangle is constructed by ASA with angles of 45 degrees and 75 degrees at the ends of the given side. What is the third angle?
mcqs.why: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees, so the third angle = 180 - 45 - 75 = 60 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.1 (p.233) - Constructing Triangles
lessons.notes_html:
Name the data before you start: SSS — draw one side, then two arcs of the other two lengths from its ends; SAS — draw one side, build the included angle, cut off the second side on the new ray; ASA — draw the side, build the given angle at each end, and the rays meet at the third vertex (the third angle is 180 minus the two given angles). In the SSA question (Q8) the arc from X cuts the ray only once inside the segment direction — the second intersection falls on the extension beyond Y, so exactly one triangle results.

In this exercise: 1. Construct a triangle ABC such that mAB = 7.5 cm, mBC = 5.5 cm and angle B = 45 degrees.. 2. Construct an isosceles triangle having each of its sides equal to 6.5 cm and the vertical angle of 60 degrees.. 3. Construct triangle ABC such that mAB = 8.3 cm, angle A = 45 degrees and angle B = 75 degrees.. 4. Construct triangle ABC such that mAB = 3.3 cm, mBC = 4.3 cm and mCA = 5.5 cm.. 5. Construct triangle ABC such that mAB = 2.5 cm, angle A = 40 degrees and angle B = 110 degrees.. 6. Construct triangle ACB, if AC = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm and angle C = 90 degrees.. 7. Construct triangle RST, if angle R = 60 degrees, RS = 7 cm and angle S = 105 degrees.. 8. Construct triangle XYZ such that XY = 4 cm, XZ = 5 cm and angle Y = 45 degrees..

Worked Example: 1. Construct a triangle ABC such that mAB = 7.5 cm, mBC = 5.5 cm and angle B = 45 degrees.

Formula used: Base first; angles built at the correct vertices; lengths cut off as arcs from the correct centres.

Step 1: draw BC = 5.5 cm.

Step 2: at B construct angle 45 degrees.

Step 3: cut off BA = 7.5 cm on the ray.

Step 4: join A with C.

Answer: triangle ABC constructed by SAS.

Worked Example: 3. Construct triangle ABC such that mAB = 8.3 cm, angle A = 45 degrees and angle B = 75 degrees.

Formula used: Base first; angles built at the correct vertices; lengths cut off as arcs from the correct centres.

Step 1: draw AB = 8.3 cm.

Step 2: at A construct angle 45 degrees and at B construct angle 75 degrees.

Step 3: the rays meet at C.

Answer: triangle ABC constructed by ASA (angle C = 60 degrees).

Worked Example: 4. Construct triangle ABC such that mAB = 3.3 cm, mBC = 4.3 cm and mCA = 5.5 cm.

Formula used: Base first; angles built at the correct vertices; lengths cut off as arcs from the correct centres.

Step 1: draw AB = 3.3 cm.

Step 2: with centre A and radius 5.5 cm, and centre B and radius 4.3 cm, draw arcs meeting at C.

Step 3: join AC and BC.

Answer: triangle ABC constructed by SSS.

Worked Example: 6. Construct triangle ACB, if AC = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm and angle C = 90 degrees.

Formula used: Base first; angles built at the correct vertices; lengths cut off as arcs from the correct centres.

Step 1: draw AC = 3 cm.

Step 2: at C construct the right angle.

Step 3: cut off CB = 4 cm on the ray.

Step 4: join A with B.

Answer: right-angled triangle ACB constructed by SAS (AB = 5 cm by Pythagoras).

Worked Example: 8. Construct triangle XYZ such that XY = 4 cm, XZ = 5 cm and angle Y = 45 degrees.

Formula used: Base first; angles built at the correct vertices; lengths cut off as arcs from the correct centres.

Step 1: at Y construct angle 45 degrees and cut off YX = 4 cm on one ray.

Step 2: with centre X and radius 5 cm draw an arc cutting the other ray at Z.

Step 3: join X with Z. Answer: one triangle XYZ (SSA case; the second intersection of the arc falls on the extension of the ray beyond Y, so it does not give a second triangle).

mcqs.q: Construct triangle ABC with mAB = 7.5 cm, mBC = 5.5 cm and angle B = 45 degrees. Which construction case is this?
mcqs.why: Two sides AB and BC are given with the angle B between them, so this is the Side-Angle-Side (SAS) case.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle ABC with mAB = 8.3 cm, angle A = 45 degrees and angle B = 75 degrees. What is angle C?
mcqs.why: Angle C = 180 - 45 - 75 = 60 degrees, which is why the two rays drawn at A and B meet to form the triangle.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle ABC with mAB = 3.3 cm, mBC = 4.3 cm and mCA = 5.5 cm. From centre B, which radius is used for the arc that locates C?
mcqs.why: In the SSS construction the arc from B has radius BC = 4.3 cm, while the arc from A has radius CA = 5.5 cm.

mcqs.q: Construct right-angled triangle ACB with AC = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm and angle C = 90 degrees. What is the length of AB?
mcqs.why: By Pythagoras, AB squared = 3 squared + 4 squared = 9 + 16 = 25, so AB = 5 cm.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle ABC with mAB = 2.5 cm, angle A = 40 degrees and angle B = 110 degrees. What is angle C?
mcqs.why: Angle C = 180 - 40 - 110 = 30 degrees, so the rays drawn at A and B meet at C in this ASA construction.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle RST with angle R = 60 degrees, RS = 7 cm and angle S = 105 degrees. What is angle T?
mcqs.why: Angle T = 180 - 60 - 105 = 15 degrees, since the three angles of any triangle add to 180 degrees.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle XYZ with XY = 4 cm, XZ = 5 cm and angle Y = 45 degrees. How many triangles does this SSA data give?
mcqs.why: The arc from X cuts the ray only once in the segment direction; the second intersection falls on the extension beyond Y, so exactly one triangle results.

mcqs.q: In the worked SAS construction with BC = 5.5 cm and angle B = 45 degrees, what is the first step?
options: Construct the 45 degree angle at C
Cut off BA = 7.5 cm on a ray
mcqs.why: The construction routine starts by drawing the base first: draw BC = 5.5 cm, then build the 45 degree angle at B.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'included' mean in the SAS construction case?
options: The given angle lies between the two given sides
The given angle is at the base of the triangle
The given angle is the largest angle
The two given sides are equal in length
mcqs.why: In SAS the given angle is the included angle, meaning it is formed by the two given sides meeting at that vertex.

mcqs.q: In an ASA construction, after drawing the given side and building the given angle at each end, how is the third vertex found?
options: An arc from the midpoint locates it
The two rays meet at the third vertex
It is marked halfway along the side
mcqs.why: In ASA the rays drawn from the two ends of the side at the given angles intersect, and their meeting point is the third vertex.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.2 (pp.236-237) - Concurrency: Bisectors, Altitudes, Perpendicular Bisectors, Medians
lessons.notes_html:
First construct the given triangle (SSS, SAS or ASA as the data require). Then draw the special lines of the exercise: angle bisectors (halve each angle with compass arcs), altitudes (perpendicular from each vertex to the opposite side), perpendicular bisectors (perpendicular at each midpoint), or medians (vertex to opposite midpoint). In every case the third line passes through the meeting point of the first two — that common point is the incentre, orthocentre, circumcentre or centroid respectively. For an obtuse triangle the circumcentre falls outside the triangle.

In this exercise: 1. Show that the angle bisectors of the given triangles are concurrent. 2. Draw altitudes of the triangle with given dimensions and show that they are concurrent. 3. Show that the perpendicular bisectors of the given triangles are concurrent. 4. Draw three medians of the following triangles and show that they are concurrent.

Worked Example: 1. Show that the angle bisectors of the given triangles are concurrent: (i) mAB = 4.7 cm, mBC = 3.6 cm and mCA = 5.4 cm.

Formula used: Construct the triangle, draw two of the special lines, mark their meeting point, then verify the third line passes through it.

Step 1: construct triangle ABC by SSS.

Step 2: draw the bisectors of angles B and C meeting at I.

Step 3: draw the bisector of angle A; it also passes through I.

Answer: the three angle bisectors are concurrent at the incentre I.

Worked Example: 2. Draw altitudes of the triangle with given dimensions and show that they are concurrent: (i) mPQ = 5.9 cm, mQR = 4.6 cm and mPR = 5.8 cm.

Formula used: Construct the triangle, draw two of the special lines, mark their meeting point, then verify the third line passes through it.

Step 1: construct triangle PQR by SSS.

Step 2: draw two altitudes meeting at O.

Step 3: draw the third altitude; it also passes through O.

Answer: the three altitudes are concurrent at the orthocentre O.

Worked Example: 3. Show that the perpendicular bisectors of the given triangles are concurrent: (i) mAB = 5.6 cm, angle A = 60 degrees, angle B = 60 degrees.

Formula used: Construct the triangle, draw two of the special lines, mark their meeting point, then verify the third line passes through it.

Step 1: construct triangle ABC by ASA (angle C = 60 degrees, so the triangle is equilateral).

Step 2: draw the perpendicular bisectors of two sides meeting at O.

Step 3: draw the perpendicular bisector of the third side; it also passes through O.

Answer: the three perpendicular bisectors are concurrent at the circumcentre O.

Worked Example: 4. Draw three medians of the following triangles and show that they are concurrent: (i) mYZ = 4.4 cm, angle Y = 45 degrees and angle Z = 75 degrees.

Formula used: Construct the triangle, draw two of the special lines, mark their meeting point, then verify the third line passes through it.

Step 1: construct triangle XYZ by ASA (angle X = 60 degrees).

Step 2: mark the midpoints of the sides and join each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Step 3: the third median also passes through the meeting point G.

Answer: the three medians are concurrent at the centroid G, dividing each other in the ratio 2 : 1.

mcqs.q: The angle bisectors of a triangle are concurrent at which point?
mcqs.why: Drawing two angle bisectors gives their meeting point I, and the third bisector also passes through the incentre I.

mcqs.q: The altitudes of a triangle are concurrent at which point?
mcqs.why: Drawing two altitudes gives their meeting point O, and the third altitude also passes through the orthocentre O.

mcqs.q: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent at which point?
mcqs.why: A perpendicular bisector is the perpendicular at the midpoint of a side, and the three of them meet at the circumcentre O.

mcqs.q: The medians of a triangle are concurrent at the centroid. In what ratio does the centroid divide each median?
mcqs.why: The three medians meet at the centroid G, which divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1.

mcqs.q: A triangle has sides mAB = 4.7 cm, mBC = 3.6 cm and mCA = 5.4 cm. By which case is it constructed before drawing its angle bisectors?
mcqs.why: All three sides are given and no angle is given, so the triangle is first constructed by the SSS case.

mcqs.q: A triangle is constructed with mAB = 5.6 cm, angle A = 60 degrees and angle B = 60 degrees. What kind of triangle is it?
mcqs.why: Angle C = 180 - 60 - 60 = 60 degrees, so all three angles are equal and the triangle is equilateral.

mcqs.q: Triangle XYZ is constructed with angle Y = 45 degrees and angle Z = 75 degrees. What is angle X?
mcqs.why: Angle X = 180 - 45 - 75 = 60 degrees in this ASA construction, before the medians are drawn.

mcqs.q: How do you show that three special lines of a triangle are concurrent?
options: Draw two of them, mark their meeting point, then check the third passes through it
Draw only one line and measure its length
Draw all three lines parallel to each other
Measure the three sides of the triangle
mcqs.why: Concurrency is shown by drawing two lines, marking their meeting point, and then verifying that the third line passes through the same point.

mcqs.q: A median of a triangle is 9 cm long. How far is the centroid from the midpoint of the opposite side?
mcqs.why: The centroid divides the median 2 : 1, so the part near the midpoint is 1/3 of 9 cm = 3 cm.

mcqs.q: For which triangle does the circumcentre fall outside the triangle?
mcqs.why: The notes state that for an obtuse triangle the circumcentre falls outside the triangle, while for an acute triangle it lies inside.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 10 (p.237)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 10: triangle names (equilateral, isosceles, scalene), the concurrency of medians, altitudes, bisectors and perpendicular bisectors, and mixed constructions drawing several special lines on one triangle.

Construct a triangle FGH where FG = 6 cm, GH = 5 cm and FH = 4.6 cm. Draw their median and verify the concurrency..

a) collinear   b) congruent   c) concurrent   d) parallel

Worked Example: Q1. (iv) The medians of a triangle divide it into ______ triangles.

a) three   b) four   c) five   d) six

Answer: d) six

Worked Example: 2. Construct triangle PQR if mPQ = 6 cm, angle P = 60 degrees, angle Q = 45 degrees. Draw median and altitude.

Formula used: See the Key Points and constructions in the Unit 10 Overview and Lessons 1 and 2 of this unit.

Step 1: construct triangle PQR by ASA (angle R = 75 degrees).

Step 2: draw a median by joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Step 3: draw an altitude by drawing the perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side.

Worked Example: 4. Construct a triangle XYZ, where mXY = 5.5 cm, angle X = 45 degrees and angle Y = 60 degrees. Also draw their perpendicular bisectors and verify the concurrency.

Worked Example: 5. Construct a triangle FGH where FG = 6 cm, GH = 5 cm and FH = 4.6 cm. Draw their median and verify the concurrency.

Formula used: See the Key Points and constructions in the Unit 10 Overview and Lessons 1 and 2 of this unit.

Step 1: construct triangle FGH by SSS.

Step 2: draw two medians meeting at G (the centroid).

Step 3: draw the third median; it also passes through the same point.

Answer: the three medians are concurrent at the centroid, dividing each other in the ratio 2 : 1.

mcqs.q: The medians of a triangle are:
mcqs.why: All three medians pass through one common point, the centroid, so the medians of a triangle are concurrent.

mcqs.q: Into how many small triangles do the three medians divide a triangle?
mcqs.why: Joining the centroid to the three vertices together with the three medians splits the triangle into six small triangles.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle PQR with mPQ = 6 cm, angle P = 60 degrees and angle Q = 45 degrees. What is angle R?
mcqs.why: Angle R = 180 - 60 - 45 = 75 degrees, so triangle PQR is constructed by the ASA case.

mcqs.q: Construct triangle XYZ with mXY = 5.5 cm, angle X = 45 degrees and angle Y = 60 degrees. What is angle Z?
mcqs.why: Angle Z = 180 - 45 - 60 = 75 degrees in this ASA construction, before the perpendicular bisectors are drawn.

mcqs.q: Triangle FGH has FG = 6 cm, GH = 5 cm and FH = 4.6 cm. By which case is it constructed?
mcqs.why: Three side lengths are given and no angle, so triangle FGH is constructed by SSS before its medians are drawn.

mcqs.q: Triangle DEF has mDE = 6 cm, angle D = 60 degrees and angle E = 60 degrees. What is angle F?
mcqs.why: Angle F = 180 - 60 - 60 = 60 degrees, so all angles are equal and triangle DEF is equilateral.

mcqs.q: A triangle in which all three sides have different lengths is called:
mcqs.why: A scalene triangle has no two sides equal, while an equilateral has all three equal and an isosceles has two equal.

mcqs.q: A triangle in which two sides are equal in length is called:
mcqs.why: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides; the angle between the equal sides in the exercise is called the vertical angle.

mcqs.q: To draw a median of a constructed triangle, you join a vertex to:
options: The opposite vertex of the triangle
The midpoint of the opposite side
Any point on the opposite side
The foot of the perpendicular from the vertex
mcqs.why: A median is defined as the segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side of the triangle.

mcqs.q: To draw an altitude of a constructed triangle, you draw:
options: A line joining two midpoints of sides
A ray halving the angle at a vertex
A line parallel to the opposite side
The perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side
mcqs.why: An altitude is the perpendicular drawn from a vertex to the opposite side, and the three altitudes meet at the orthocentre.

lessons.title: Unit 11 Overview — Frequency, Averages and Probability
lessons.notes_html:
Statistics organises raw data into classes. The range is maximum - minimum; the class interval is the range divided by the number of classes, rounded up to a convenient size. The frequency of a class is the number of values in it, and the cumulative frequency is the running total. A histogram draws bars over the class boundaries with heights equal to the frequencies.

Formula: Mean (direct) = (sum of values) / n ; for grouped data, Mean = sum of (f x midpoint) / sum of f.

Formula: Indirect (assumed-mean) method: Mean = a + (sum of deviations from a) / n, where a is a chosen central value.

Key Points

  • Median = the middle value of the ordered data (the average of the two middle values when n is even). For grouped data: Median = L + (h / f) x (n/2 - cf), where L is the lower boundary of the median class, h its width, f its frequency and cf the cumulative frequency before it.
  • Mode = the most frequently occurring value. For grouped data: Mode = L + h x (f1 - f0) / ((f1 - f0) + (f1 - f2)), using the modal class and its two neighbours.
  • Weighted mean = (sum of value x weight) / (sum of weights) — used when the values count unequally, as in the average price per kg in Exercise 11.2 Q6.
  • A single very low or very high value pulls the mean towards it but leaves the median almost unchanged — choose the median when the data has such an outlier (Exercise 11.3 Q5).
  • Probability: for equally likely outcomes, P(E) = n(E) / n(S), where S is the sample space of all outcomes. Every probability lies between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). Tree diagrams list the outcomes of combined trials; a Venn diagram shows overlaps such as "odd AND greater than 3".
  • Relative frequency = frequency / total trials — the experimental estimate of a probability. Expected frequency in N new trials = relative frequency x N.

Formula: P(E) = n(E) / n(S) ; Relative frequency = f / N ; Expected frequency = relative frequency x N.

mcqs.q: The values in a data set run from a minimum of 16 to a maximum of 55. What is the range?
mcqs.why: Range = maximum - minimum = 55 - 16 = 39, which is the first step in organising raw data into classes.

mcqs.q: A range of 57 is to be split into 6 classes. What class interval is taken?
mcqs.why: Class interval = range / number of classes = 57 / 6 = 9.5, which is rounded up to the convenient size 10.

mcqs.q: Frequencies of three classes are 4, 8 and 15. What is the cumulative frequency up to the second class?
mcqs.why: Cumulative frequency is a running total: after the second class it is 4 + 8 = 12 (and 27 after the third class).

mcqs.q: Find the mean of 8, 12, 10, 14 and 16 by the direct method.
mcqs.why: Mean = sum of values / n = (8 + 12 + 10 + 14 + 16) / 5 = 60 / 5 = 12 by the direct method.

mcqs.q: Find the median of the ordered data 3, 5, 7, 9.
mcqs.why: With n = 4 (even), the median is the average of the two middle values: (5 + 7) / 2 = 6.

mcqs.q: Find the mode of 4, 6, 6, 8, 6, 9.
mcqs.why: The mode is the most frequently occurring value: 6 occurs three times, more than any other value in the list.

mcqs.q: For grouped data, each class is represented in the mean formula by which value?
options: The lower limit of the class
The upper limit of the class
mcqs.why: Grouped mean = sum of (f x midpoint) / sum of f, so every class is represented by its midpoint.

mcqs.q: In the weighted mean formula, the sum of (value x weight) is divided by:
mcqs.why: Weighted mean = (sum of value x weight) / (sum of weights), used when the values count unequally.

mcqs.q: A die is rolled once. Using a Venn diagram idea, what is the probability of getting a number that is odd AND greater than 3?
mcqs.why: The sample space is {1,2,3,4,5,6}; the only number both odd and greater than 3 is 5, so P = 1/6.

mcqs.q: A data set contains one very low value that drags the average down. Which average is least affected by this outlier?
mcqs.why: A single very low or high value pulls the mean towards it but leaves the median almost unchanged, so the median is chosen.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.1 (p.246) - Frequency Distributions and Histograms
lessons.notes_html:
To tabulate raw data: find the minimum and maximum, choose the number of classes (or the class width the question gives), and set the class interval = range / number of classes, rounded up. Count the values into each class with tally marks, check that the frequencies add to the total number of values, then build the cumulative frequency as a running total. For a histogram, use the true class boundaries (16-25 becomes 15.5-25.5) on the horizontal axis and draw touching bars whose heights are the frequencies.

In this exercise: 1. The following is a record of weights of 40 students in pounds (lbs). Tabulate the data in the form of frequency distribution by taking 6 classes. Also find cumulative frequency. The following data give the index numbers of 45 commodities in a certain year: 120, 138, 113, 119, 111, 118, 123, 151, 134, 141, 115, 119, 124, 112, 145, 114, 106, 112, 110, 106, 111, 153, 100, 101, 108, 133, 100, 109, 110, 143, 109, 138, 113, 136, 100, 104, 144, 128, 105, 106, 147, 127, 140, 129, 108.. 4. Data: 72, 96, 69, 78, 76, 112, 93, 107, 73, 61, 75, 91, 106, 84, 103, 109, 96, 88, 80, 86, 90, 105, 77, 90, 101, 91, 102, 92, 91, 82, 99, 63, 95, 118, 77, 72, 114, 101, 113, 105.
