mcqs.q: Weights of 40 students: minimum = 61 lbs and maximum = 118 lbs. What is the range?
mcqs.why: Range = maximum - minimum = 118 - 61 = 57 lbs, before the class interval 57/6 = 9.5 is taken as 10.

mcqs.q: In the weights distribution (classes 60-69: 3; 70-79: 8; 80-89: 5; 90-99: 11; 100-109: 9; 110-119: 4), what is the frequency of the class 90-99?
mcqs.why: Counting the tally marks for weights from 90 to 99 lbs gives 11 students, the largest frequency in the table.

mcqs.q: Using the same weights distribution, what is the cumulative frequency up to the class 80-89?
mcqs.why: Cumulative frequency is the running total: 3 + 8 + 5 = 16 up to and including the class 80-89.

mcqs.q: In the weights distribution of 40 students, what is the total of all the class frequencies?
mcqs.why: The frequencies must add to the number of values: 3 + 8 + 5 + 11 + 9 + 4 = 40 students.

mcqs.q: Marks of 50 students are grouped in classes of width 5. The class 75-79 has the highest bar in the histogram. What is its frequency?
mcqs.why: In the marks distribution the class 75-79 contains 11 students, more than any other class, so its histogram bar is tallest.

mcqs.q: For the marks data of 50 students, the minimum mark is 53 and the maximum is 97. In which class does the mark 53 fall when classes of width 5 start at 50-54?
mcqs.why: The first class of width 5 is 50-54, and 53 lies inside it; this class has frequency 1 in the distribution.

mcqs.q: For a histogram, the class 16-25 is drawn over which true class boundaries?
mcqs.why: For a histogram the class 16-25 becomes the true boundaries 15.5-25.5, so the touching bars have no gaps between them.

mcqs.q: In the histogram data (16-25: 4; 26-35: 8; 36-45: 15; 46-55: 7; 56-65: 6), which class has the tallest bar?
mcqs.why: Bar heights equal the frequencies, and 36-45 has the greatest frequency, 15 students, so its bar is the tallest.

mcqs.q: In the same histogram data, how many students are there in total?
mcqs.why: Total frequency = 4 + 8 + 15 + 7 + 6 = 40 students, which checks the frequency table before drawing the histogram.

mcqs.q: What does the height of each bar in a histogram represent?
options: The class interval of the class
mcqs.why: A histogram draws bars over the class boundaries with heights equal to the frequencies of the classes.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.2 (pp.252-253) - Mean, Median and Mode
lessons.notes_html:
The mean by the direct method is the total divided by the count; the indirect method picks an assumed mean a, adds the average deviation, and gives the same answer with smaller numbers. For grouped data, each class is represented by its midpoint: mean = sum(f x midpoint) / sum(f).

The median is the middle value after ordering; for grouped data use the median-class formula from the Overview. The mode is the commonest value, or the modal-class formula for grouped data. Q6 is a weighted mean (price per kg weighted by kg bought). Honest notes from the data: in Q4 the grouped frequencies total 58 although the survey says 60 adults, and in Q7 the family table totals 136 although its heading says 127 — the calculations follow the frequencies as printed.

Formula: Mean = sum(f x) / sum(f) with x = class midpoint ; Median = L + (h/f)(n/2 - cf) ; Mode = L + h(f1 - f0)/((f1 - f0) + (f1 - f2))

In this exercise: 1. Find arithmetic mean by (a) direct method (b) indirect method for the following data. 2. Find arithmetic mean of the following marks obtained by students of 10th class in a test: classes 25-29: 8; 30-34: 13; 35-39: 19; 40-44: 14; 45-49: 10; 50-54: 4.. 3. Find mean, median and mode of the runs scored by 11 players: 45, 58, 61, 35, 29, 37, 58, 55, 48, 57, 42.. 4. A health survey recorded the weights (in pounds) of 60 adults in a factory and grouped them as follows: 65-84: 3; 85-104: 8; 105-124: 19; 125-144: 14; 145-164: 9; 165-184: 5. Find median and mode of the above data.. 5. A teacher records final exam marks of 100 students grouped as: 10-19: 5; 20-29: 25; 30-39: 40; 40-49: 20; 50-59: 10. Find the mean, median and mode of the above data.. 6. A person purchased the following food items: Rice 10 kg at Rs.2500 per kg; Flour 13 kg at Rs.1950 per kg; Ghee 15 kg at Rs.2200 per kg; Sugar 4 kg at Rs.520 per kg; Mutton 3 kg at Rs.5500 per kg. What is the average cost of food items per kg?. 7. Following table lists the size of families: size 2: 4; 3: 50; 4: 35; 5: 27; 6: 13; 7: 5; 8: 2. Calculate mean, median and mode. NOTE: the table heading says 127 families, but the frequencies add to 136; the calculations use the frequencies as printed..

Worked Example: 1. Find arithmetic mean by (a) direct method (b) indirect method for the following data: (i) 15, 29, 25, 18, 45, 34, 39, 32, 41, 26.

Formula used: Grouped mean uses midpoints; median and mode use the median/modal class formulas in the Overview.

Step 1: (a) direct: sum = 304, n = 10, mean = 304/10 = 30.4.

Step 2: (b) indirect: take assumed mean a = 30; deviations sum to 4; mean = 30 + 4/10 = 30.4.

Answer: mean = 30.4.

Worked Example: 2. Find arithmetic mean of the following marks obtained by students of 10th class in a test: classes 25-29: 8; 30-34: 13; 35-39: 19; 40-44: 14; 45-49: 10; 50-54: 4.

Formula used: Grouped mean uses midpoints; median and mode use the median/modal class formulas in the Overview.

Step 1: midpoints are 27, 32, 37, 42, 47, 52.

Step 2: sum f = 68; sum fx = 216 + 416 + 703 + 588 + 470 + 208 = 2601.

Step 3: mean = 2601/68 = 38.25.

Answer: mean = 38.25.

Worked Example: 3. Find mean, median and mode of the runs scored by 11 players: 45, 58, 61, 35, 29, 37, 58, 55, 48, 57, 42.

Formula used: Grouped mean uses midpoints; median and mode use the median/modal class formulas in the Overview.

Step 1: mean = 525/11 = 47.73.

Step 2: in ascending order: 29, 35, 37, 42, 45, 48, 55, 57, 58, 58, 61; median (6th value) = 48.

Step 3: 58 occurs twice, more than any other value.

Answer: mean = 47.73; median = 48; mode = 58.

Worked Example: 5. A teacher records final exam marks of 100 students grouped as: 10-19: 5; 20-29: 25; 30-39: 40; 40-49: 20; 50-59: 10. Find the mean, median and mode of the above data.

Formula used: Grouped mean uses midpoints; median and mode use the median/modal class formulas in the Overview.

Step 1: midpoints 14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5, 54.5; sum fx = 72.5 + 612.5 + 1380 + 890 + 545 = 3500; mean = 3500/100 = 35.

Step 2: cumulative frequencies 5, 30, 70, 90, 100; median class 30-39: median = 29.5 + (10/40)(50 - 30) = 34.5.

Step 3: modal class 30-39: mode = 29.5 + (40 - 25) x 10/((40 - 25) + (40 - 20)) = 33.79.

Answer: mean = 35; median = 34.5; mode = 33.79.

Worked Example: 6. A person purchased the following food items: Rice 10 kg at Rs.2500 per kg; Flour 13 kg at Rs.1950 per kg; Ghee 15 kg at Rs.2200 per kg; Sugar 4 kg at Rs.520 per kg; Mutton 3 kg at Rs.5500 per kg. What is the average cost of food items per kg?

Formula used: Grouped mean uses midpoints; median and mode use the median/modal class formulas in the Overview.

Step 1: total quantity = 10 + 13 + 15 + 4 + 3 = 45 kg.

Step 2: total cost = 25000 + 25350 + 33000 + 2080 + 16500 = 101930.

Step 3: average cost = 101930/45 = 2265.11.

Answer: Rs.2265.11 per kg (weighted mean).

mcqs.q: Find the mean of 15, 29, 25, 18, 45, 34, 39, 32, 41, 26 by the direct method.
For the same data, the indirect method takes assumed mean a = 30 and the deviations add to 4. What mean does it give?
mcqs.why: Indirect method: mean = a + (sum of deviations)/n = 30 + 4/10 = 30 + 0.4 = 30.4, the same as the direct method.
Midpoints 27, 32, 37, 42, 47, 52 give sum fx = 2601 and sum f = 68, so mean = 2601 / 68 = 38.25.

mcqs.q: What is the midpoint of the class 35-39 in that grouped marks distribution?
mcqs.why: Midpoint = (35 + 39) / 2 = 74 / 2 = 37, and this midpoint represents the whole class in the grouped mean.

mcqs.q: Runs scored by 11 players: 45, 58, 61, 35, 29, 37, 58, 55, 48, 57, 42. What is the mean?
mcqs.why: Sum of runs = 525 and n = 11, so mean = 525 / 11 = 47.73 (to two decimal places).

mcqs.q: For the same 11 players' runs, what is the median?
mcqs.why: Ordered runs: 29, 35, 37, 42, 45, 48, 55, 57, 58, 58, 61; the middle (6th) value is 48, so the median is 48.

mcqs.q: For the same 100 students' marks, what is the median?
mcqs.why: Cumulative frequencies are 5, 30, 70, 90, 100; median class is 30-39, so median = 29.5 + (10/40)(50 - 30) = 34.5.

mcqs.q: For the same 100 students' marks, what is the mode?
Food bought: Rice 10 kg at Rs.2500/kg; Flour 13 kg at Rs.1950/kg; Ghee 15 kg at Rs.2200/kg; Sugar 4 kg at Rs.520/kg; Mutton 3 kg at Rs.5500/kg. What is the average cost per kg?
mcqs.why: Total cost = 25000+25350+33000+2080+16500 = 101930 and total quantity = 45 kg, so weighted mean = 101930 / 45 = Rs.2265.11 per kg.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.3 (pp.255-256) - Working with Averages
lessons.notes_html:
These questions run the average formulas in reverse: a combined mean gives an equation for an unknown group mean (total = mean x count for each group); a given median and mode fix two missing values by ordering the list; and unknown frequencies x and y are found from two equations — the total frequency and the total of the values (the mean). Q5 compares the three averages on real score sets: the mean can be dragged by one low score where the median cannot.

In this exercise: 1. The mean of a set of 6 numbers is 2 and the mean of another set of 10 numbers is x. If the mean of all 16 numbers is 7, find the value of x.. 2. The numbers 24, 22, 34, 28, 29, 24, 25, 29, a and b have a median of 27 and a mode of 29. Given that a < b, state the value of a and of b.. 3. 2000 people responded to the blood bank's appeal for blood donors. The blood type, i.e. A, B, AB or O, of each donor is recorded: A: h; B: 800; AB: 200; O: k. (a). 4. A box contains five cards numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. A card is drawn from the box, its number noted and then replaced. The process is repeated 100 times. The table shows the resulting frequency distribution: card 1: 21; 2: x; 3: y; 4: 18; 5: 17.. 5. Three netball teams each played five games. Scores: Cheetah 65, 95, 32, 96, 88; Jaguar 50, 90, 65, 87, 87; Puma 90, 85, 46, 44, 80. (a).

Worked Example: 1. The mean of a set of 6 numbers is 2 and the mean of another set of 10 numbers is x. If the mean of all 16 numbers is 7, find the value of x.

Formula used: Totals first: sum = mean x n for each group; order the list for median/mode conditions; solve the pair of equations for unknown frequencies.

Step 1: sum of the first set = 6 x 2 = 12; sum of the second set = 10x.

Step 2: (12 + 10x)/16 = 7, so 12 + 10x = 112 and 10x = 100.

Answer: x = 10.

Worked Example: 2. The numbers 24, 22, 34, 28, 29, 24, 25, 29, a and b have a median of 27 and a mode of 29. Given that a < b, state the value of a and of b.

Formula used: Totals first: sum = mean x n for each group; order the list for median/mode conditions; solve the pair of equations for unknown frequencies.

Step 1: with a = 26 and b = 29 the sorted list is 22, 24, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29, 29, 29, 34.

Step 2: median = (26 + 28)/2 = 27.

Step 3: 29 occurs three times, more than any other value.

Answer: a = 26, b = 29.

Worked Example: 4. A box contains five cards numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. A card is drawn from the box, its number noted and then replaced. The process is repeated 100 times. The table shows the resulting frequency distribution: card 1: 21; 2: x; 3: y; 4: 18; 5: 17. (i) Show that x + y = 44. (ii) If the mean of the distribution is 2.9, show that 2x + 3y = 112. (iii) Hence, find the value of x and of y.

Formula used: Totals first: sum = mean x n for each group; order the list for median/mode conditions; solve the pair of equations for unknown frequencies.

Step 1: (i) total frequency: 21 + x + y + 18 + 17 = 100, so x + y = 44.

Step 2: (ii) total of values = 21 + 2x + 3y + 72 + 85 = 178 + 2x + 3y = 2.9 x 100 = 290, so 2x + 3y = 112.

Step 3: (iii) subtracting twice (i) from (ii): y = 24, so x = 20.

Answer: (i) x + y = 44; (ii) 2x + 3y = 112; (iii) x = 20, y = 24.

Worked Example: 5. Three netball teams each played five games. Scores: Cheetah 65, 95, 32, 96, 88; Jaguar 50, 90, 65, 87, 87; Puma 90, 85, 46, 44, 80. (a) (i) By considering the mean score of each team, which team would you join? Justify by showing working. (ii) If instead you base your decision on the median score of each team, which team would you join? Justify by showing working. (b) Suppose you are the coach of Team Jaguar and are being interviewed about your team for the local newspaper. Would it be better to report the mean score or the median score of your team? Explain your answer.

Formula used: Totals first: sum = mean x n for each group; order the list for median/mode conditions; solve the pair of equations for unknown frequencies.

Step 1: (a) (i) means: Cheetah 376/5 = 75.2; Jaguar 379/5 = 75.8; Puma 345/5 = 69.0. Jaguar has the highest mean.

Step 2: (a) (ii) medians: Cheetah 88; Jaguar 87; Puma 80. Cheetah has the highest median.

Step 3: (b) Jaguar's mean (75.8) is pulled down by the one low score of 50, while its median (87) reflects the team's usual level; reporting the median is better and more representative.

Answer: (a) (i) Jaguar; (a) (ii) Cheetah; (b) the median, because the mean is dragged down by the single low score of 50.

mcqs.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 2 and the mean of another 10 numbers is x. The mean of all 16 numbers is 7. Find x.
mcqs.why: Totals: first set sums to 6 x 2 = 12; (12 + 10x)/16 = 7 gives 12 + 10x = 112, so 10x = 100 and x = 10.

mcqs.q: The numbers 24, 22, 34, 28, 29, 24, 25, 29, a and b have median 27 and mode 29, with a < b. What is the value of a?
mcqs.why: With a = 26 and b = 29 the ordered list is 22, 24, 24, 25, 26, 28, 29, 29, 29, 34, giving median (26+28)/2 = 27.

mcqs.q: In the same question (median 27, mode 29, a < b), what is the value of b?
mcqs.why: Taking b = 29 makes 29 occur three times, more than any other value, so the mode is 29 as required.

mcqs.q: Cards 1 to 5 are drawn with replacement 100 times: frequencies are 1: 21; 2: x; 3: y; 4: 18; 5: 17. What is x + y?
mcqs.why: Total frequency: 21 + x + y + 18 + 17 = 100, so x + y = 100 - 56 = 44.

mcqs.q: For the same card experiment the mean of the distribution is 2.9. Which equation follows from the mean?
Solving x + y = 44 together with 2x + 3y = 112 for the card experiment, what is x?
mcqs.why: Subtracting twice x + y = 44 from 2x + 3y = 112 gives y = 24, and then x = 44 - 24 = 20.

mcqs.q: In the same card experiment, what is y?
mcqs.why: From 2x + 3y = 112 minus 2(x + y) = 88, we get y = 112 - 88 = 24, and x = 44 - 24 = 20 checks the total.

mcqs.q: Netball scores: Cheetah 65, 95, 32, 96, 88. What is Cheetah's mean score?
mcqs.why: Cheetah's total = 65 + 95 + 32 + 96 + 88 = 376 over 5 games, so the mean = 376 / 5 = 75.2.

mcqs.q: Netball means: Cheetah 75.2, Jaguar 75.8, Puma 69.0. Judged by the mean, which team should you join?
mcqs.why: Jaguar's mean = 379 / 5 = 75.8, which is higher than Cheetah's 75.2 and Puma's 69.0, so Jaguar is best by the mean.

mcqs.q: Jaguar's coach reports one average for the newspaper. Jaguar's scores are 50, 90, 65, 87, 87. Which average is better to report, and why?
options: The mean, because it uses every score equally well
The median, because the mean is dragged down by the low score of 50
The mode, because it is the largest score
The mean, because the low score raises it
mcqs.why: Jaguar's median is 87 but the mean is only 379/5 = 75.8, pulled down by the single low score of 50, so the median is more representative.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.4 (p.263) - Probability
lessons.notes_html:
Write the sample space first: 4 outcomes for two coins, 36 for two dice, 8 for three children. Count the favourable outcomes carefully — for dice sums and products a 6 x 6 table helps — then P(E) = n(E) / n(S), simplified. "At least" and "at most" are often quickest by the complement: P(at least one girl) = 1 - P(no girl). "Or" adds the counts when the events cannot overlap; "not green" = 1 - P(green).

Formula: P(E) = n(E) / n(S) ; P(not E) = 1 - P(E)

In this exercise: 1. Two fair coins are tossed. Find the probability of getting. 2. Two dice, one red and the other green, are rolled simultaneously. The numbers of dots on the tops are added. Find the probability of getting a sum of. 3. A bag contains 30 balls out of which 6 are green, 10 are red and the remaining are black. A ball is drawn out of the bag. Find the probability of getting. 4. A die is rolled. Find the probability by Venn diagram of getting. 5. In a three child family, what is the probability (by using tree diagram) of. 6. In a single throw of two fair dice, find the probability that the product of the numbers on the dice is. 7. A marble is drawn at random from a box containing 30 red, 10 white, 20 orange and 15 blue marbles. Find the probability that it is. 8. Two coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting.

Worked Example: 1. Two fair coins are tossed. Find the probability of getting (i) at most one head; (ii) same faces.

Formula used: List the sample space, count the favourable outcomes, divide, simplify; use the complement for at-least/at-most.

Step 1: sample space S = {HH, HT, TH, TT}, n(S) = 4.

Step 2: (i) at most one head: {HT, TH, TT}, probability 3/4.

Step 3: (ii) same faces: {HH, TT}, probability 2/4 = 1/2.

Answer: (i) 3/4; (ii) 1/2.

Worked Example: 2. Two dice, one red and the other green, are rolled simultaneously. The numbers of dots on the tops are added. Find the probability of getting a sum of: (i) 7; (ii) 9; (iii) 12.

Formula used: List the sample space, count the favourable outcomes, divide, simplify; use the complement for at-least/at-most.

Step 1: n(S) = 36.

Step 2: (i) sum 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) = 6 outcomes, probability 6/36 = 1/6.

Step 3: (ii) sum 9: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) = 4 outcomes, probability 4/36 = 1/9.

Step 4: (iii) sum 12: (6,6) = 1 outcome, probability 1/36.

Answer: (i) 1/6; (ii) 1/9; (iii) 1/36.

Worked Example: 3. A bag contains 30 balls out of which 6 are green, 10 are red and the remaining are black. A ball is drawn out of the bag. Find the probability of getting: (i) the ball is green; (ii) the ball is black; (iii) the ball is not green.

Formula used: List the sample space, count the favourable outcomes, divide, simplify; use the complement for at-least/at-most.

Step 1: black balls = 30 - 6 - 10 = 14.

Step 2: (i) P(green) = 6/30 = 1/5.

Step 3: (ii) P(black) = 14/30 = 7/15.

Step 4: (iii) P(not green) = 24/30 = 4/5.

Answer: (i) 1/5; (ii) 7/15; (iii) 4/5.

Worked Example: 5. In a three child family, what is the probability (by using tree diagram) of: (i) three girls; (ii) exactly two boys; (iii) at least one girl.

Formula used: List the sample space, count the favourable outcomes, divide, simplify; use the complement for at-least/at-most.

Step 1: sample space has 8 outcomes: BBB, BBG, BGB, BGG, GBB, GBG, GGB, GGG.

Step 2: (i) three girls: {GGG}, probability 1/8.

Step 3: (ii) exactly two boys: {BBG, BGB, GBB}, probability 3/8.

Step 4: (iii) at least one girl: all except BBB, probability 7/8.

Answer: (i) 1/8; (ii) 3/8; (iii) 7/8.

Worked Example: 7. A marble is drawn at random from a box containing 30 red, 10 white, 20 orange and 15 blue marbles. Find the probability that it is: (i) orange or red; (ii) not blue or red; (iii) red, white or blue.

Formula used: List the sample space, count the favourable outcomes, divide, simplify; use the complement for at-least/at-most.

Step 1: total = 75.

Step 2: (i) orange or red: (20 + 30)/75 = 50/75 = 2/3.

Step 3: (ii) 'not blue or red' is read as neither blue nor red: white or orange = (10 + 20)/75 = 30/75 = 2/5 (the event 'not blue' alone would be 60/75 = 4/5).

Step 4: (iii) red, white or blue: (30 + 10 + 15)/75 = 55/75 = 11/15.

Answer: (i) 2/3; (ii) 2/5 (neither blue nor red); (iii) 11/15.

mcqs.q: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at most one head?
mcqs.why: Sample space {HH, HT, TH, TT} has 4 outcomes; at most one head gives {HT, TH, TT}, so P = 3/4.

mcqs.q: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting the same faces?
mcqs.why: Same faces are {HH, TT}, which is 2 of the 4 outcomes in the sample space, so P = 2/4 = 1/2.

mcqs.q: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability of getting a sum of 7?
Two dice are rolled. What is the probability of getting a sum of 9?
mcqs.why: Sum 9 comes from (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3): 4 outcomes out of 36, so P = 4/36 = 1/9.

mcqs.q: A bag has 30 balls: 6 green, 10 red and the rest black. How many black balls are there?
mcqs.why: Black balls = 30 - 6 - 10 = 14, which is needed before finding any probability for the black balls.

mcqs.q: From the same bag of 30 balls (6 green, 10 red, 14 black), what is the probability of drawing a black ball?
mcqs.why: P(black) = number of black balls / total balls = 14/30, which simplifies to 7/15.

mcqs.q: From the same bag of 30 balls, what is the probability of drawing a ball that is not green?
mcqs.why: Not green = 30 - 6 = 24 balls, so P(not green) = 24/30 = 4/5, also found as 1 - P(green) = 1 - 1/5.

mcqs.q: In a three-child family, what is the probability of three girls?
mcqs.why: The tree diagram gives 8 outcomes: BBB, BBG, BGB, BGG, GBB, GBG, GGB, GGG; only GGG is three girls, so P = 1/8.

mcqs.q: In a three-child family, what is the probability of exactly two boys?
mcqs.why: Exactly two boys gives {BBG, BGB, GBB}: 3 outcomes out of the 8 in the sample space, so P = 3/8.

mcqs.q: A box has 30 red, 10 white, 20 orange and 15 blue marbles. What is the probability of drawing an orange or a red marble?
mcqs.why: Total = 75 marbles; orange or red = 20 + 30 = 50, so P = 50/75, which simplifies to 2/3.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.5 (p.266) - Relative and Expected Frequency
lessons.notes_html:
Relative frequency = frequency / total number of trials; the relative frequencies of all outcomes add to 1, which also finds a missing one. To predict: expected frequency = relative frequency x the new number of trials N. The same rule reads a probability backwards — a biased coin with P(tail) = 0.45 gives expected tails = 0.45 x tosses.

Formula: Relative frequency = f / N ; Expected frequency = relative frequency x N

In this exercise: 1. Calculate relative frequencies and expected frequencies of the following data, where N = 400: Marks 31-40: 5; 41-50: 9; 51-60: 15; 61-70: 12; 71-80: 9. Also find. 2. A tin contains some biscuits. The flavours of the biscuits and the amount of each flavor are shown in the table: Chocolate 14; Lemon 16; Ginger 28; Caramel 8. Find. 3. A biased coin is tossed 500 times and probability of tail is 0.45. Find the expected frequency of occurring head and tail.. 4. Find the expected frequencies of the following data, where N = 512: x: 0: 5; 1: 6; 2: 15; 3: 4; 4: 2.. 5. A spinner was spun 50 times, and it landed on red 12 times. What is the relative frequency of the spinner landing on red?. 6. A survey of 200 people showed that 60 prefer chocolate ice cream. What is the expected number of people who would prefer chocolate ice cream out of a group of 500?. 7. A factory machine produced 400 items out of which 16 were defective. What is the relative frequency of producing a defective item?.

Worked Example: 1. Calculate relative frequencies and expected frequencies of the following data, where N = 400: Marks 31-40: 5; 41-50: 9; 51-60: 15; 61-70: 12; 71-80: 9. Also find (i) P(X >= 60); (ii) P(X <= 50).

Formula used: Divide each frequency by the total for relative frequencies; multiply by the new N for expected frequencies.

Step 1: total = 50; relative frequencies: 5/50 = 0.10; 9/50 = 0.18; 15/50 = 0.30; 12/50 = 0.24; 9/50 = 0.18.

Step 2: expected frequencies (N = 400): 40, 72, 120, 96, 72.

Step 3: (i) P(X >= 60) = (12 + 9)/50 = 0.42 (classes wholly above 60).

Step 4: (ii) P(X <= 50) = (5 + 9)/50 = 0.28.

Answer: relative frequencies 0.10, 0.18, 0.30, 0.24, 0.18; expected frequencies 40, 72, 120, 96, 72; (i) 0.42; (ii) 0.28.

Worked Example: 2. (i) Find the relative frequencies of the data: Colour Red: 35/100; Green: (blank); Yellow: 5/100. (ii) Find probability of not red.

Formula used: Divide each frequency by the total for relative frequencies; multiply by the new N for expected frequencies.

Step 1: relative frequencies add to 1, so Green = 1 - 0.35 - 0.05 = 0.60 = 60/100.

Step 2: (ii) P(not red) = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65.

Answer: (i) Red 0.35, Green 0.60, Yellow 0.05; (ii) 0.65.

Worked Example: 4. A biased coin is tossed 500 times and probability of tail is 0.45. Find the expected frequency of occurring head and tail.

Formula used: Divide each frequency by the total for relative frequencies; multiply by the new N for expected frequencies.

Step 1: expected tails = 500 x 0.45 = 225.

Step 2: P(head) = 1 - 0.45 = 0.55; expected heads = 500 x 0.55 = 275.

Answer: heads 275; tails 225.

Worked Example: 5. Find the expected frequencies of the following data, where N = 512: x: 0: 5; 1: 6; 2: 15; 3: 4; 4: 2.

Formula used: Divide each frequency by the total for relative frequencies; multiply by the new N for expected frequencies.

Step 1: total = 32; relative frequencies: 5/32, 6/32, 15/32, 4/32, 2/32.

Step 2: expected frequencies: 512 x 5/32 = 80; 512 x 6/32 = 96; 512 x 15/32 = 240; 512 x 4/32 = 64; 512 x 2/32 = 32.

Answer: 80, 96, 240, 64, 32.

mcqs.q: Marks data: 31-40: 5; 41-50: 9; 51-60: 15; 61-70: 12; 71-80: 9 (total 50). What is the relative frequency of the class 51-60?
mcqs.why: Relative frequency = frequency / total trials = 15 / 50 = 0.30 for the class 51-60.

mcqs.q: For the same marks data, what is the expected frequency of the class 51-60 in N = 400 new trials?
mcqs.why: Expected frequency = relative frequency x N = 0.30 x 400 = 120 for the class 51-60.

mcqs.q: For the same marks data (total 50), using relative frequencies, what is P(X >= 60)?
mcqs.why: Classes wholly above 60 are 61-70 and 71-80 with frequencies 12 + 9 = 21, so P(X >= 60) = 21/50 = 0.42.

mcqs.q: Relative frequencies of colours are Red 35/100, Yellow 5/100 and Green unknown. What is the relative frequency of Green?
mcqs.why: Relative frequencies add to 1, so Green = 1 - 0.35 - 0.05 = 0.60, i.e. 60/100.

mcqs.q: Using Red's relative frequency of 0.35, what is the probability of not red?
mcqs.why: P(not red) = 1 - P(red) = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65, using the relative frequency as the probability estimate.

mcqs.q: A biased coin is tossed 500 times and P(tail) = 0.45. What is the expected frequency of tails?
mcqs.why: Expected frequency = probability x number of tosses = 0.45 x 500 = 225 tails.

mcqs.q: For the same biased coin tossed 500 times with P(tail) = 0.45, what is the expected frequency of heads?
mcqs.why: P(head) = 1 - 0.45 = 0.55, so expected heads = 0.55 x 500 = 275 (and 275 + 225 = 500 checks the total).

mcqs.q: Data: x = 0: 5; 1: 6; 2: 15; 3: 4; 4: 2 (total 32). With N = 512, what is the expected frequency of x = 2?
mcqs.why: Relative frequency of x = 2 is 15/32, so expected frequency = 512 x 15/32 = 16 x 15 = 240.

mcqs.q: A spinner was spun 50 times and landed on red 12 times. What is the relative frequency of red?
mcqs.why: Relative frequency = frequency / total trials = 12 / 50 = 0.24 for the spinner landing on red.

mcqs.q: A survey of 200 people showed 60 prefer chocolate ice cream. How many would be expected to prefer it in a group of 500?
mcqs.why: Relative frequency = 60/200 = 0.30, so expected number = 0.30 x 500 = 150 people.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 11 (p.267)
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 11: histograms and cumulative frequency, mean/median/mode for raw and grouped data, probability from sample spaces, and relative frequency.

In this exercise: 1. Choose the correct options. 2. Find the mean, median and mode of the marks of 10 students in a test of Mathematics (out of 50): 45, 32, 36, 48, 45, 24, 28, 35, 46, 40.. 3. Find arithmetic mean, median and mode of the following data: classes 36-40: 9; 41-45: 16; 46-50: 24; 51-55: 15; 56-60: 10; 61-65: 8.. 4. A coin is tossed 3 times. Find the probability of. 5. Find relative frequency of the data: Group 51-60: 3; 61-70: 8; 71-80: 15; 81-90: 9; 91-100: 4..

Worked Example: Q1. (iii) In a distribution, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, the mean is:

a) 75   b) 15   c) 30   d) 45

Answer: b) 15

Worked Example: Q1. (v) Probability of an event lies between:

a) -1 and 1   b) -1 and 0   c) 0 and 1   d) -0.5 to 0.5

Answer: c) 0 and 1

Worked Example: 2. Find the mean, median and mode of the marks of 10 students in a test of Mathematics (out of 50): 45, 32, 36, 48, 45, 24, 28, 35, 46, 40.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 11 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: mean = 379/10 = 37.9.

Step 2: in ascending order: 24, 28, 32, 35, 36, 40, 45, 45, 46, 48; median = (36 + 40)/2 = 38.

Step 3: 45 occurs twice, more than any other value.

Answer: mean = 37.9; median = 38; mode = 45.

Worked Example: 3. Find arithmetic mean, median and mode of the following data: classes 36-40: 9; 41-45: 16; 46-50: 24; 51-55: 15; 56-60: 10; 61-65: 8.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 11 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: midpoints 38, 43, 48, 53, 58, 63; sum f = 82; sum fx = 342 + 688 + 1152 + 795 + 580 + 504 = 4061; mean = 4061/82 = 49.52.

Step 2: cumulative frequencies 9, 25, 49, 64, 74, 82; median class 46-50: median = 45.5 + (5/24)(41 - 25) = 48.83.

Step 3: modal class 46-50: mode = 45.5 + (24 - 16) x 5/((24 - 16) + (24 - 15)) = 47.85.

Answer: mean = 49.52; median = 48.83; mode = 47.85.

Worked Example: 4. A coin is tossed 3 times. Find the probability of (i) at least two heads; (ii) at the most two tails.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 11 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: sample space has 8 outcomes.

Step 2: (i) at least two heads: {HHH, HHT, HTH, THH}, probability 4/8 = 1/2.

Step 3: (ii) at most two tails: all except TTT, probability 7/8.

Answer: (i) 1/2; (ii) 7/8.

Worked Example: 5. Find relative frequency of the data: Group 51-60: 3; 61-70: 8; 71-80: 15; 81-90: 9; 91-100: 4.

Formula used: See the Key Points and formulas in the Unit 11 Overview and Lessons 1 to 5 of this unit.

Step 1: total = 39.

Step 2: relative frequencies: 3/39 = 0.08; 8/39 = 0.21; 15/39 = 0.38; 9/39 = 0.23; 4/39 = 0.10 (approx).

Answer: 0.08, 0.21, 0.38, 0.23, 0.10.

mcqs.q: In the distribution 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, the mean is:
mcqs.why: Mean = sum / n = (15 x 5) / 5 = 75 / 5 = 15, since every value in the distribution is 15.

mcqs.q: The probability of an event lies between:
mcqs.why: Every probability lies between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain), as P(E) = n(E)/n(S) with n(E) at most n(S).

mcqs.q: Marks of 10 students: 45, 32, 36, 48, 45, 24, 28, 35, 46, 40. What is the mean?
mcqs.why: Sum of marks = 379 and n = 10, so mean = 379 / 10 = 37.9 marks out of 50.

mcqs.q: For the same 10 students' marks, what is the median?
mcqs.why: Ordered marks: 24, 28, 32, 35, 36, 40, 45, 45, 46, 48; median = average of the two middle values = (36 + 40)/2 = 38.

mcqs.q: For the same 10 students' marks, what is the mode?
mcqs.why: The value 45 occurs twice in the marks list, more than any other value, so the mode is 45.
Midpoints 38, 43, 48, 53, 58, 63 give sum fx = 4061 and sum f = 82, so mean = 4061 / 82 = 49.52.

mcqs.q: For the same grouped data, what is the median?
mcqs.why: Cumulative frequencies 9, 25, 49, 64, 74, 82; median class 46-50, so median = 45.5 + (5/24)(41 - 25) = 48.83.

mcqs.q: A coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least two heads?
mcqs.why: The 8 outcomes include at least two heads in {HHH, HHT, HTH, THH}: 4 outcomes, so P = 4/8 = 1/2.

mcqs.q: Groups: 51-60: 3; 61-70: 8; 71-80: 15; 81-90: 9; 91-100: 4. What is the relative frequency of the group 71-80?
mcqs.why: Total frequency = 3 + 8 + 15 + 9 + 4 = 39, so relative frequency of 71-80 = 15/39 = 0.38 (approx).

mcqs.q: For the same groups (total 39), what is the relative frequency of the group 51-60?
mcqs.why: Relative frequency = frequency / total = 3/39 = 0.08 (approx) for the group 51-60.
